title.zh: 卷九十九 列傳第八十七: 突厥 鐵勒
title.raw: 卷九十九 列傳第八十七: 突厥 鐵勒 Volume 99 Biographies 87: Tujie, Tiele

sentences.zh: 突厥 鐵勒

translations.literal: Turks; Tiele
translations.idiomatic: The Turks and the Tiele

sentences.zh: 突厥者，其先居西海之右，獨為部落，蓋匈奴之別種也。

translations.literal: As for the Turks, their ancestors dwelt to the west of the Western Sea, forming a tribe by themselves; they were probably a separate branch of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks: their forebears lived west of the Western Sea as an independent tribe, likely a distinct offshoot of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 姓阿史那氏。

translations.literal: Their surname was the Ashina clan.
translations.idiomatic: They bore the clan name Ashina.

sentences.zh: 後為鄰國所破，盡滅其族。

translations.literal: Later they were destroyed by a neighboring state, and the entire clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Later a neighboring power overran them and wiped out the whole clan.

sentences.zh: 有一兒，年且十歲，兵人見其小，不忍殺之，乃刖足斷其臂，棄草澤中。

translations.literal: There was one boy, about ten years old; the soldiers, seeing how small he was, could not bear to kill him, so they cut off his feet and severed his arms and abandoned him in the marsh grass.
translations.idiomatic: One boy of about ten was spared because the soldiers thought him too young to kill; instead they maimed his feet and arms and left him in the wild marshes.

sentences.zh: 有牝狼以肉餌之，及長，與狼交合，遂有孕焉。

translations.literal: A she-wolf fed him with meat; when he grew up, he mated with the wolf, and she became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: A she-wolf brought him meat; when he came of age he coupled with her, and she conceived.

sentences.zh: 彼王聞此兒尚在，重遣殺之。

translations.literal: That king, hearing the boy was still alive, again sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When that king learned the boy still lived, he sent assassins once more.

sentences.zh: 使者見在狼側，並欲殺狼。

translations.literal: The envoys saw him beside the wolf and wished to kill the wolf as well.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys found him at the wolf's side and meant to slay the beast too.

sentences.zh: 于時若有神物，投狼於西海之東，落高昌國西北山。

translations.literal: At that moment, as if by a divine being, the wolf was cast to the east of the Western Sea and fell on a mountain northwest of the state of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Then, as though some spirit intervened, the wolf was hurled east of the Western Sea onto a peak northwest of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 山有洞穴，穴內有平壤茂草，周迥數百里，四面俱山。

translations.literal: On the mountain was a cave; inside the cave was level ground with lush grass, extending for several hundred li on every side, mountains on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain held a cavern enclosing level ground and rich pasture, hundreds of li across, ringed by peaks on every side.

sentences.zh: 狼匿其中，遂生十男。

translations.literal: The wolf hid therein and thereafter bore ten sons.
translations.idiomatic: The wolf sheltered there and in time gave birth to ten sons.

sentences.zh: 十男長，外托妻孕，其後各為一姓，阿史那即其一也，最賢，遂為君長。

translations.literal: When the ten sons grew up, they took wives from outside and had children; afterward each became a separate clan. Ashina was one of them, the most worthy, and thus became the chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: The ten sons grew up, married women from outside, and each founded a clan; Ashina was among them, the most able, and became their leader.

sentences.zh: 故牙門建狼頭纛，示不忘本也。

translations.literal: Therefore at the royal encampment they set up a wolf-head banner, to show they did not forget their origin.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the royal tent flies a wolf-head standard, a reminder that they have not forgotten their roots.

sentences.zh: 漸至數百家，經數世，有阿賢設者，率部落出於穴中，臣於蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Gradually they reached several hundred households; after several generations there was one named Ashina Xianshe, who led the tribe out of the cave and submitted to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: They grew to several hundred families; generations later Ashina Xianshe led the tribe forth from the cave and submitted to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 至大葉護，種類漸強。

translations.literal: By the time of Dayehu, the people gradually grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dayehu their people grew steadily stronger.

sentences.zh: 當魏之末，有伊利可汗，以兵擊鐵勒，大敗之，降五萬餘家。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei there was the Yili Qaghan, who attacked the Tiele with troops, utterly defeated them, and received the submission of more than fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Wei, Yili Qaghan marched against the Tiele, routed them, and brought more than fifty thousand households to submission.

sentences.zh: 遂求婚於蠕蠕主。

translations.literal: He then sought marriage with the Rouran ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked the Rouran khan for a bride.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰大怒，遣使罵之。

translations.literal: Anagui was greatly angered and sent envoys to revile him.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui flew into a rage and sent envoys to heap abuse on him.

sentences.zh: 伊利斬其使，率眾襲蠕蠕，破之。

translations.literal: Yili beheaded the envoys, led his host in a surprise attack on the Rouran, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yili executed the envoys, led his warriors in a raid on the Rouran, and broke their power.

sentences.zh: 卒，弟阿逸可汗立，又破蠕蠕。

translations.literal: When he died, his younger brother Ayi Qaghan succeeded and again defeated the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his brother Ayi Qaghan took the throne and again defeated the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 病且卒，舍其子攝圖，立其弟俟叔稱為木杆可汗。

translations.literal: When he fell ill and was near death, he set aside his son Shetu and installed his younger brother Hou Shu, who took the title Mugan Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he passed over his son Shetu and installed his younger brother Hou Shu as Mugan Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 或云突厥本平涼雜胡，姓阿史那氏。

translations.literal: Some say the Turks were originally miscellaneous Hu from Pingliang, surnamed Ashina.
translations.idiomatic: Another account holds that the Turks were originally mixed barbarians of Pingliang of the Ashina clan.

sentences.zh: 魏太武皇帝滅沮渠氏，阿史那以五百家奔蠕蠕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu of Wei destroyed the Juqu clan, the Ashina fled to the Rouran with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu of Wei destroyed the Juqu, five hundred Ashina households fled to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 世居金山之陽，為蠕蠕鐵工。

translations.literal: For generations they dwelt south of Mount Jin and served the Rouran as ironworkers.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they lived south of Mount Jin, smithing iron for the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 金山形似兜鍪，俗號兜鍪為突厥，因以為號。

translations.literal: Mount Jin resembled a helmet; in common speech a helmet was called tujue, and from this they took their name.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Jin looked like a helmet; the common word for helmet was tujue, and from that they took their name.

sentences.zh: 又曰突厥之先，出於索國，在匈奴之北。

translations.literal: It is also said that the ancestors of the Turks came from the state of Suo, north of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Another tradition places the Turkic forebears in the land of Suo, north of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 其部落大人曰阿謗步，兄弟七十人，其一曰伊質泥師都，狼所生也。

translations.literal: The great man of their tribe was called Abolu; he had seventy brothers, one of whom was named Yizhi Nishidu, born of a wolf.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribal lord was Abolu, who had seventy brothers; one of them, Yizhi Nishidu, was said to be wolf-born.

sentences.zh: 阿謗卻等性並愚癡，國遂被滅。

translations.literal: Abolu and the others were all foolish by nature, and their state was therefore destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Abolu and his kin were all dull-witted, and their realm was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 泥師都既別感異氣，能征占風雨。

translations.literal: Nishidu, having separately received a strange emanation, could divine and control wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Nishidu was touched by a strange power and could read and command the weather.

sentences.zh: 取二妻，雲是夏神、冬神之女。

translations.literal: He took two wives, said to be daughters of the gods of summer and winter.
translations.idiomatic: He married two wives, said to be daughters of the summer and winter gods.

sentences.zh: 一孕而生四男：其一變為白鴻；

translations.literal: From one pregnancy four sons were born: the first transformed into a white swan;
translations.idiomatic: One pregnancy yielded four sons: the first became a white swan;

sentences.zh: 其一國于阿輔水、劍水之間，號為契骨；

translations.literal: one founded a state between the Afu and Jian Rivers, called Qigu;
translations.idiomatic: one founded a realm between the Afu and Jian rivers, called Qigu;

sentences.zh: 其一國于處折水；

translations.literal: one founded a state on the Chuzhe River;
translations.idiomatic: one settled on the Chuzhe River;

sentences.zh: 其一居跋斯處折施山，即其大兒也。

translations.literal: one dwelt on Mount Basichuzheshi—that was the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: one lived on Mount Basichuzheshi—the eldest son.

sentences.zh: 山上仍有阿謗步種類，並多寒露，大兒為出火溫養之，咸得全濟。

translations.literal: On the mountain the people of Abolu's kind still remained; there was much cold dew, and the eldest son made fire to warm and nurture them, and all were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Abolu's people still lived on the mountain, suffering from cold dew; the eldest son kindled fires to warm them, and all were saved.

sentences.zh: 遂共奉大兒為主，號為突厥，即納都六設也。

translations.literal: They then together made the eldest son their lord, calling him Turk—that is, Nadulu She.
translations.idiomatic: They together enthroned the eldest son as their lord, naming him Turk—Nadulu She.

sentences.zh: 都六有十妻，所生子皆以母族姓，阿史那是其小妻之子也。

translations.literal: Dulu had ten wives; the sons born to him all took their mothers' clan names. Ashina was the son of his youngest wife.
translations.idiomatic: Dulu had ten wives; each son took his mother's clan name. Ashina was born of the youngest wife.

sentences.zh: 都六死，十母子內欲擇立一人，乃相率於大樹下，共為約曰：「向樹跳躍，能最高者，即推立之。」

translations.literal: When Dulu died, the ten mothers and sons within wished to choose one to install; they therefore led one another under a great tree and made a pact, saying: 'Leap toward the tree; whoever can leap highest shall be installed.'
translations.idiomatic: When Dulu died, the ten mothers and sons wished to choose a leader; they gathered under a great tree and agreed: 'Whoever leaps highest toward the tree shall be our chief.'

sentences.zh: 阿史那子年幼而跳最高，諸子遂奉以為主，號阿賢設。

translations.literal: The Ashina boy, though young, leaped highest; the sons therefore installed him as lord, with the title Ashina Xianshe.
translations.idiomatic: The young Ashina boy leaped highest, and the sons installed him as their lord, titled Ashina Xianshe.

sentences.zh: 此說雖殊，終狼種也。

translations.literal: Although these accounts differ, in the end they are wolf stock.
translations.idiomatic: The tales differ, but in the end they are all wolf-born.

sentences.zh: 其後曰土門，部落稍盛，始至塞上市繒絮，願通中國。

translations.literal: Later there was Tumen; the tribe gradually flourished and for the first time came to the frontier markets to sell silk floss, wishing to communicate with China.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Tumen; as the tribe grew, they first brought silk floss to the frontier markets, seeking trade with China.

sentences.zh: 西魏大統十一年，周文帝遣酒泉胡安諾槃陀使焉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Datong of Western Wei, Emperor Wen of Zhou sent the Jiuquan Hu Anuopantuo as envoy there.
translations.idiomatic: In Western Wei's Datong year 11, Emperor Wen of Zhou sent the Jiuquan Hu Anuopantuo as envoy.

sentences.zh: 其國皆相慶曰：「今大國使至，我國將興也。」

translations.literal: Throughout the state they congratulated one another, saying: 'Now an envoy from the great state has come; our state will rise.'
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm rejoiced: 'An envoy from the great power has come—our realm will flourish.'

sentences.zh: 十二年，土門遂遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Tumen sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Tumen sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 時鐵勒將伐蠕蠕，土門率所部邀擊破之，盡降其眾五萬餘落。

translations.literal: At that time the Tiele were about to attack the Rouran; Tumen led his division in an intercepting attack and defeated them, receiving the submission of their entire host of more than fifty thousand clans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tiele were marching on the Rouran, Tumen ambushed and routed them, bringing more than fifty thousand clans to submission.

sentences.zh: 恃其強盛，乃求婚於蠕蠕主。

translations.literal: Relying on his strength, he then sought marriage with the Rouran ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by his strength, he asked the Rouran khan for a bride.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰大怒，使人詈辱之曰：「爾是我鍛奴，何敢發是言也！」

translations.literal: Anagui was greatly angered and sent a man to revile and humiliate him, saying: 'You are my iron-smithing slave—how dare you utter such words!'
translations.idiomatic: Anagui was furious and sent a man to insult him: 'You are my blacksmith slave—how dare you speak such words!'

sentences.zh: 土門亦怒，殺其使者，遂與之絕，而求婚于魏。

translations.literal: Tumen was also angered; he killed the envoy, broke with them, and sought marriage with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Tumen in turn killed the envoy, broke with the Rouran, and sought a Wei bride.

sentences.zh: 周文帝許之，十七年六月，以魏長樂公主妻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou granted it; in the sixth month of the seventeenth year he gave him Princess Changle of Wei in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou agreed; in the sixth month of year 17 he gave him Princess Changle of Wei in marriage.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏文帝崩，土門遣使來吊，贈馬二百疋。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Wen of Wei died; Tumen sent envoys to offer condolences and presented two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Wen of Wei died; Tumen sent envoys to mourn him and presented two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元年正月，土門發兵擊蠕蠕，大破之於懷荒北。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Emperor Fei, Tumen raised troops and attacked the Rouran, utterly defeating them north of Huaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Emperor Fei's first year, Tumen marched on the Rouran and routed them north of Huaihuang.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰自殺，其子庵羅辰奔齊，餘眾復立阿那瑰叔父鄧叔子為主。

translations.literal: Anagui killed himself; his son Anluochen fled to Qi, and the remaining host again installed Anagui's uncle Deng Shuzi as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui took his own life; his son Anluochen fled to Qi, and the survivors enthroned Anagui's uncle Deng Shuzi.

sentences.zh: 土門遂自號伊利可汗，猶古之單于也；

translations.literal: Tumen then styled himself Yili Qaghan, like the ancient shanyu;
translations.idiomatic: Tumen then took the title Yili Qaghan, in the manner of the ancient shanyu;

sentences.zh: 號其妻為可賀敦，亦猶古之閼氏也。

translations.literal: he styled his wife Kehedun, also like the ancient yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: his wife he called Kehedun, as the ancient yanzhi had been styled.

sentences.zh: 亦與齊通使往來。

translations.literal: He also exchanged envoys with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He also exchanged envoys with Qi.

sentences.zh: 土門死，子科羅立。

translations.literal: When Tumen died, his son Keluo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tumen died; his son Keluo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 科羅號乙息記可汗，又破叔子于沃野北賴山。

translations.literal: Keluo took the title Yixiji Qaghan and again defeated Shuzi at Mount Beilai north of Woye.
translations.idiomatic: Keluo styled himself Yixiji Qaghan and again defeated Shuzi at Mount Beilai north of Woye.

sentences.zh: 且死，舍其子攝圖，立其弟俟斤，是為木杆可汗。

translations.literal: When he was near death he set aside his son Shetu and installed his younger brother Houjin, who became Mugan Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he passed over his son Shetu and installed his brother Houjin as Mugan Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 俟斤一名燕都，狀貌奇異，面廣尺餘，其色赤甚，眼若琉璃，剛暴，勇而多知，務於征伐。

translations.literal: Houjin, also named Yandu, had a strange appearance: his face was more than a foot wide, exceedingly red in color, his eyes like glass; he was fierce and violent, brave and knowledgeable, devoted to campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Houjin, also called Yandu, had a striking appearance—a face more than a foot across, deeply flushed, eyes like glass; fierce, brave, and shrewd, he lived for war.

sentences.zh: 乃率兵擊鄧叔子，破之。

translations.literal: He then led troops to attack Deng Shuzi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Deng Shuzi and broke him.

sentences.zh: 叔子以其餘燼奔西魏。

translations.literal: Shuzi fled to Western Wei with his remaining embers.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzi fled to Western Wei with his shattered remnant.

sentences.zh: 俟斤又西破嚈噠，東走契丹，北並契骨，威服塞外諸國。

translations.literal: Houjin again defeated the Yeda in the west, drove the Khitan eastward, annexed Qigu in the north, and by his might brought the states beyond the frontier to submission.
translations.idiomatic: Houjin crushed the Yeda in the west, drove the Khitan east, absorbed Qigu in the north, and by force brought the frontier realms to heel.

sentences.zh: 其地，東自遼海以西，至西海，萬里；

translations.literal: His territory: from east of the Liao Sea westward to the Western Sea, ten thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: His domain stretched ten thousand li from east of the Liao Sea west to the Western Sea;

sentences.zh: 南自沙漠以北，至北海，五六千里：皆屬焉。

translations.literal: from south of the desert northward to the Northern Sea, five or six thousand li—all belonged to him.
translations.idiomatic: and from south of the desert north to the Northern Sea, five or six thousand li—all fell under his rule.

sentences.zh: 抗衡中國，後與魏伐齊，至并州。

translations.literal: He contended on equal terms with China; later he joined Wei in attacking Qi and reached Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He stood as China's equal; later he joined Wei against Qi and reached Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其俗：被髮左衽，穹廬氈帳，隨逐水草遷徙，以畜牧射獵為事，食肉飲酪，身衣裘褐。

translations.literal: Their customs: they wore their hair loose and closed their robes on the left; they lived in domed felt tents, migrating with the grass and water; their occupation was herding livestock and hunting; they ate meat and drank fermented milk, and clothed themselves in furs and coarse cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs: loose hair and left-lapped robes; domed felt tents; they followed grass and water; herding and hunting were their livelihood; they ate meat, drank kumis, and wore furs and coarse wool.

sentences.zh: 賤老貴壯，寡廉恥，無禮義，猶古之匈奴。

translations.literal: They despised the old and honored the strong; they had little sense of shame or propriety, no ritual or righteousness—like the ancient Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: They scorned age and prized strength; shame and ritual meant little to them—much like the ancient Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 其主初立，近侍重臣等輿之以氈，隨日轉九回，每回臣下皆拜，拜訖乃扶令乘馬，以帛絞其頸，使才不至絕，然後釋而急問之曰：「你能作幾年可汗？」

translations.literal: When their ruler was first installed, close attendants and great ministers carried him on felt, turning with the sun nine circuits; at each circuit the ministers all bowed; when the bowing was finished they helped him mount a horse, strangled his neck with silk so that he was nearly but not quite dead, then released him and urgently asked: 'How many years can you be qaghan?'
translations.idiomatic: When a new qaghan was enthroned, his close ministers carried him on felt, turning nine times with the sun; at each turn the court bowed. Then they helped him mount, throttled his neck with silk until he nearly died, released him, and urgently asked: 'How many years will you reign?'

sentences.zh: 其主既神情瞀亂，不能詳定多少。

translations.literal: The ruler, his spirit already confused and dim, could not specify how many.
translations.idiomatic: Dazed by the ordeal, the qaghan could give no clear number.

sentences.zh: 臣下等隨其所言，以驗修短之數。

translations.literal: The ministers followed whatever he said to verify the length of his allotted span.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he blurted out, the court took as the measure of his allotted reign.

sentences.zh: 大官有葉護，次設，次特勤，次俟利發，次吐屯發，及餘小官，凡二十八等，皆世為之。

translations.literal: Great offices included yehu, she, teqin, houlife, and tutunfa, along with other lesser offices—in all twenty-eight ranks, all hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: Great offices included yehu, she, teqin, houlife, and tutunfa, with lesser ranks besides—twenty-eight grades in all, all hereditary.

sentences.zh: 兵器有角弓、鳴鏑、甲、槊、刀、劍、佩飾則兼有伏突。

translations.literal: Their weapons included horn bows, whistling arrows, armor, spears, knives, and swords; for personal adornment they also wore futu daggers.
translations.idiomatic: They bore horn bows, whistling arrows, armor, spears, knives, and swords, and wore futu daggers at the belt.

sentences.zh: 旗纛之上，施金狼頭。

translations.literal: On their banners and standards they affixed gilded wolf heads.
translations.idiomatic: Their banners bore gilded wolf heads.

sentences.zh: 待衛之士謂之附離，夏言亦狼也。

translations.literal: The guards were called fuli; in Chinese this also means 'wolf.'
translations.idiomatic: The royal guard were called fuli—'wolf' in their tongue.

sentences.zh: 蓋本狼生，志不忘舊。

translations.literal: This was because they were originally wolf-born, their hearts not forgetting their origin.
translations.idiomatic: Born of the wolf, they would not forget their origins.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，性殘忍。

translations.literal: They were skilled at mounted archery and cruel by nature.
translations.idiomatic: They excelled at mounted archery and were cruel by nature.

sentences.zh: 無文字，其徵發兵馬及諸稅雜畜，刻木為數，並一金鏃箭，蠟封印之，以為信契。

translations.literal: They had no writing; for levying troops and horses and various taxes in livestock they carved wood for numbers, and together with a gold-tipped arrow sealed it with wax as a token of trust.
translations.idiomatic: They had no script; levies of men, horses, and livestock were tallied on carved wood, sealed with wax on a gold-tipped arrow as their bond.

sentences.zh: 候月將滿，轉為寇抄。

translations.literal: When they awaited the moon nearing fullness, they turned to raiding and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: As the moon waxed full, they turned to raiding.

sentences.zh: 其刑法：反叛、殺人、及奸人之婦、盜馬絆者，皆死；

translations.literal: Their penal code: rebellion, murder, adultery with another man's wife, and theft of horse hobbles—all were capital;
translations.idiomatic: Their law: rebellion, murder, adultery with another man's wife, and theft of horse hobbles—all carried the death penalty;

sentences.zh: 淫者，割勢而腰斬之；

translations.literal: for fornication they cut off the genitals and cut the body in two at the waist;
translations.idiomatic: fornicators were castrated and cut in two at the waist;

sentences.zh: 奸人女者，重責財物，即以其女妻之；

translations.literal: for seducing another man's daughter they imposed heavy fines in goods and gave him the daughter in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: seducers of another man's daughter paid a heavy fine and received the girl as wife;

sentences.zh: 鬥傷人者，隨輕重輸物，傷目者償以女，無女則輸婦財，折支體者輸馬；

translations.literal: for brawling and injuring others they paid goods according to severity; for injuring an eye they compensated with a daughter, and if there was no daughter they paid bride-price goods; for breaking limbs they paid horses;
translations.idiomatic: assault was compensated in goods by severity; blinding an eye cost a daughter, or bride-price if there was no daughter; broken limbs cost horses;

sentences.zh: 盜馬及雜物者，各十餘倍征之。

translations.literal: for theft of horses and miscellaneous goods they levied more than ten times the value.
translations.idiomatic: horse theft and petty theft were fined at more than ten times the value.

sentences.zh: 死者，停屍於帳，子孫及親屬男女各殺羊、馬，陳於帳前祭之，繞帳走馬七匝，詣帳門以刀剺面且哭，血淚俱流，如此者七度乃止。

translations.literal: When someone died, the corpse was laid in the tent; sons, grandsons, and male and female kin each killed sheep and horses and set them before the tent as offerings; they circled the tent on horseback seven rounds, came to the tent door, cut their faces with knives and wept, blood and tears flowing together—this they did seven times before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: When someone died, the body lay in the tent while kin slaughtered sheep and horses as offerings; they circled the tent seven times on horseback, then at the door cut their faces with knives until blood and tears mingled—seven rounds of this mourning.

sentences.zh: 擇日，取亡者所乘馬及經服用之物，並屍俱焚之，收其餘灰，待時而葬。

translations.literal: On a chosen day they took the deceased's riding horse and garments he had worn, burned them together with the corpse, gathered the remaining ashes, and awaited the proper time for burial.
translations.idiomatic: On a chosen day they burned the dead man's horse, clothing, and corpse together, gathered the ashes, and waited for the proper season to bury them.

sentences.zh: 春夏死者，候草木黃落；

translations.literal: For those who died in spring or summer, they waited until the grass and trees yellowed and fell;
translations.idiomatic: For spring and summer deaths they waited until the grass yellowed;

sentences.zh: 秋冬死者，候華茂，然後坎而痤之。

translations.literal: for those who died in autumn or winter, they waited until flowers and foliage flourished, then dug a pit and buried the ashes.
translations.idiomatic: autumn and winter deaths waited until bloom returned, then buried the ashes in a pit.

sentences.zh: 葬日，親屬設祭及走馬、剺面如初死之儀。

translations.literal: On the burial day, kin set out offerings and performed the horse-circling and face-cutting as at the first death rites.
translations.idiomatic: On burial day kin repeated the offerings, horse-circling, and face-cutting of the first mourning.

sentences.zh: 表為塋，立屋，中圖畫死者形儀，及其生時所戰陣狀，嘗殺一人，則立一石，有致千百者。

translations.literal: They marked a grave mound, erected a house, and inside painted the deceased's likeness and the battle formations of his lifetime; for each person he had killed in life they set up one stone—some had hundreds or thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They raised a mound and a house painted with the dead man's likeness and his battles; for each man he had killed in life they set a stone—some graves had hundreds or thousands.

sentences.zh: 又以祭之羊、馬頭，盡懸之於標上。

translations.literal: They also hung all the sheep and horse heads from the sacrifice on poles.
translations.idiomatic: The sheep and horse heads from the sacrifice they hung on poles.

sentences.zh: 是日也，男女咸盛服飾，會於葬所，男有悅愛於女者，歸即遣人聘問，其父母多不違也。

translations.literal: On that day men and women all wore splendid dress and gathered at the burial place; if a man took a liking to a woman, upon returning he sent someone to propose, and the parents mostly did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: That day men and women dressed in their finest and gathered at the grave; if a man fancied a woman, he sent a matchmaker on his return, and parents rarely refused.

sentences.zh: 父、兄、伯、叔死，子、弟及侄等妻其後母、世叔母、嫂，唯尊者不得下淫。

translations.literal: When father, elder brother, paternal uncle, or maternal uncle died, sons, younger brothers, and nephews took as wives the stepmother, uncle's widow, or sister-in-law—only those of higher rank might not take inferiors in lewd union.
translations.idiomatic: On a father's, elder brother's, or uncle's death, sons, younger brothers, and nephews might marry the widow—stepmother, uncle's wife, or sister-in-law—save that the senior might not debauch his inferiors.

sentences.zh: 移徙無常，而各有地分。

translations.literal: Their migrations had no fixed pattern, yet each had his allotted territory.
translations.idiomatic: They moved without fixed abode, yet each clan held its allotted ground.

sentences.zh: 可汁恆處於都斤山，牙帳東開，蓋敬日之所出也。

translations.literal: The qaghan always resided at Mount Dujin; the royal tent opened to the east, presumably in reverence for where the sun rises.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan dwelt on Mount Dujin; the royal tent faced east, honoring the sunrise.

sentences.zh: 每歲率諸貴人，祭其先窟。

translations.literal: Each year he led the nobles to sacrifice at their ancestral cave.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he led the nobles to sacrifice at the ancestral cave.

sentences.zh: 又以五月中旬，集他人水拜祭天神。

translations.literal: Also in mid-fifth month they gathered at another's waters to bow and sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-fifth month they gathered at shared waters to worship Heaven.

sentences.zh: 於都斤西五百里有高山迥出，上無草樹、謂為勃登凝梨，夏言地神也。

translations.literal: Five hundred li west of Dujin a high mountain rose abruptly, with no grass or trees on it; they called it Bodengningli—in Chinese, the Earth God.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li west of Dujin stood a bare peak they called Bodengningli—the Earth God in their tongue.

sentences.zh: 其書字類胡，而不知年曆，唯以草青為記。

translations.literal: Their script resembled that of the Hu, but they did not know the calendar; they reckoned only by when the grass turned green.
translations.idiomatic: Their script resembled foreign writing, but they knew no calendar—only the greening of the grass marked the year.

sentences.zh: 男子好樗蒲，女子踏鞠，飲馬酪取醉，歌呼相對。

translations.literal: Men loved to play chupu; women played cuju; they drank mare's milk until drunk and sang and shouted to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Men loved dice; women played cuju; they drank kumis to drunkenness and sang and shouted face to face.

sentences.zh: 敬鬼神，信巫覡，重兵死，恥病終，大抵與匈奴同俗。

translations.literal: They revered ghosts and spirits, trusted shamans, honored death in battle, and were ashamed to die of illness—in general their customs were the same as the ancient Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: They revered spirits, trusted shamans, honored death in battle and shamed death by sickness—in most respects their ways matched the ancient Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 俟斤部眾既盛，乃遣使請誅鄧叔子等，周文帝許之，收叔子已下三千人，付其使者，殺之於青門外。

translations.literal: When Houjin's tribes had grown strong, he sent envoys requesting the execution of Deng Shuzi and others; Emperor Wen of Zhou granted it, seized Deng Shuzi and those below him, three thousand persons, handed them to the envoys, and they were killed outside the Qing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: As Houjin's following grew mighty, he asked Zhou to execute Deng Shuzi and his party; Emperor Wen agreed, seized Shuzi and three thousand of his men, handed them to the Turk envoys, and they were put to death outside the Qing Gate.

sentences.zh: 三年，俟斤襲擊吐谷渾破之。

translations.literal: In the third year Houjin raided the Tuyuhun and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Houjin raided the Tuyuhun and routed them.

sentences.zh: 周明帝二年，俟斤遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Ming of Zhou, Houjin sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming of Zhou's second year, Houjin sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，又遣三輩，貢其方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding he again sent three missions, presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding he sent three missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 時與齊人交爭，戎車歲動，故連結之，以為外援。

translations.literal: At that time they were locked in conflict with the Qi, and war chariots moved every year; therefore they allied with the Turks as an external aid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was then at war with Qi year after year, and courted the Turks as allies beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 初，恭帝時，俟斤許進女于周文帝，契未定而周文崩。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the time of Emperor Gong, Houjin had promised to send a daughter to Emperor Wen of Zhou; the pact was not settled when Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Emperor Gong, Houjin had promised a daughter to Emperor Wen of Zhou, but the pact was unsettled when Wen died.

sentences.zh: 尋而俟斤又以他女許武帝，未及結納，齊人亦遣求婚，俟斤貪其幣厚，將悔之。

translations.literal: Soon after Houjin again promised another daughter to Emperor Wu; before the marriage was concluded, the Qi also sent to propose marriage, and Houjin, coveting their rich gifts, was about to repent of the Zhou match.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Houjin promised another daughter to Emperor Wu; before the match was sealed, Qi also proposed, and Houjin, tempted by Qi's lavish gifts, nearly reneged on Zhou.

sentences.zh: 至是，武帝詔遣涼州刺史楊薦、武伯王慶等往結之。

translations.literal: At this point Emperor Wu ordered Liangzhou Inspector Yang Jian, Wubo Wang Qing, and others to go and conclude the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu then sent Liangzhou Inspector Yang Jian, Wubo Wang Qing, and others to seal the alliance.

sentences.zh: 慶等至，諭以信義，俟斤遂絕齊使而訂婚焉。

translations.literal: When Qing and the others arrived, they expounded trust and righteousness; Houjin then cut off the Qi envoys and fixed the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and his party arrived, spoke of trust and duty, and Houjin broke with Qi and confirmed the Zhou marriage.

sentences.zh: 仍請舉國東伐，於是詔隨公楊忠率眾一萬與突厥伐齊。

translations.literal: He further asked to lead the whole state east in campaign; thereupon an edict ordered Duke Sui Yang Zhong to lead ten thousand men with the Turks against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to march the whole nation east; the court ordered Duke Sui Yang Zhong to lead ten thousand men with the Turks against Qi.

sentences.zh: 忠軍度陘嶺，侯斤率騎十萬來會。

translations.literal: Zhong's army crossed the Long Ridge; Houjin led one hundred thousand horsemen to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's army crossed the Long Ridge; Houjin brought one hundred thousand horsemen to the rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，攻齊主于晉陽，不克，俟斤遂縱兵大掠而還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year they attacked the Qi ruler at Jinyang but did not take it; Houjin then let his troops plunder on a great scale and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next first month they besieged the Qi ruler at Jinyang without success; Houjin then unleashed his men to plunder and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 忠還，言于武帝曰：「突厥甲兵惡，賞罰輕，首領多而無法令，何謂難制馭？

translations.literal: When Zhong returned, he said to Emperor Wu: 'The Turks' armor and weapons are fierce, but rewards and punishments are light; there are many chiefs and no laws—why call them hard to control?
translations.idiomatic: On his return Zhong told Emperor Wu: 'Turk arms are fierce, but their rewards and punishments are slight; they have many chiefs and no real law—why call them hard to govern?

sentences.zh: 由比者使人妄道其強盛，欲令國家厚其使者，身往重取其報。

translations.literal: It is because former envoys falsely spoke of their strength, wishing the state to enrich their envoys while they themselves went and took heavy rewards in return.
translations.idiomatic: Former envoys lied about their strength so the court would lavish gifts on them while they pocketed heavy rewards abroad.

sentences.zh: 朝廷受其虛言，將士望風畏懾。

translations.literal: The court accepted their empty words, and officers and soldiers feared them at mere rumor.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed their boasts, and our soldiers quailed at the mere rumor of them.

sentences.zh: 但虜態詐健，而實易與耳。

translations.literal: The barbarians are only crafty and bold in appearance; in truth they are easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians look cunning and bold, but in truth they are easy to handle.

sentences.zh: 今以臣觀之，前後使人皆可斬也。」

translations.literal: In my view, envoys before and after could all be beheaded.'
translations.idiomatic: In my view, every envoy who lied about them deserves the axe.'

sentences.zh: 武帝不納。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 是歲，俟斤復遣使來獻，更請東伐。

translations.literal: That year Houjin again sent envoys with tribute and again requested an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: That year Houjin sent tribute again and asked for another eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔楊忠率兵出沃野，晉公護趣洛陽以應之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yang Zhong to lead troops out from Woye; Duke Jin Hu hurried to Luoyang to support him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Yang Zhong out from Woye and Duke Jin Hu to Luoyang in support.

sentences.zh: 會護戰不利，俟斤引還。

translations.literal: When Hu's battle went ill, Houjin withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu's campaign faltered, Houjin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔陳公純、大司徒宇文貴、神武公竇毅、南安公楊薦往逆女。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict ordered Duke Chen Chun, Grand Minister of Education Yuwen Gui, Duke Shenwu Dou Yi, and Duke Nan'an Yang Jian to go and escort the bride.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the court sent Duke Chen Chun, Grand Minister Yuwen Gui, Duke Shenwu Dou Yi, and Duke Nan'an Yang Jian to escort the bride.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，俊斤又遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, Houjin again sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 2 Houjin again sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 陳公純等至，俟斤復貳于齊。

translations.literal: When Duke Chen Chun and the others arrived, Houjin again wavered toward Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Chen Chun arrived, Houjin wavered toward Qi once more.

sentences.zh: 會有雷風變，乃許純等以後歸。

translations.literal: When thunder and wind changed, he then promised Chun and the others she would return later.
translations.idiomatic: After thunder and wind omens, he promised Chun that the bride would follow later.

sentences.zh: 四年，又遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 俟斤死，復舍其子大邏便而立其弟，是為他缽可汗。

translations.literal: When Houjin died, he again set aside his son Daluobian and installed his younger brother, who became Tabo Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Houjin died; again a son was passed over—Daluobian—and a younger brother installed as Tabo Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 他缽以攝圖為爾伏可汗，統其東面；

translations.literal: Tabo made Shetu Erfu Qaghan, commanding the eastern sector;
translations.idiomatic: Tabo made Shetu Erfu Qaghan over the east;

sentences.zh: 又以其弟褥但可汗為步離可汗，居西方。

translations.literal: he also made his younger brother Rutan Qaghan Buli Qaghan, dwelling in the west.
translations.idiomatic: and his brother Rutan Buli Qaghan over the west.

sentences.zh: 自俟斤以來，其國富強，有淩轢中夏之志。

translations.literal: From Houjin onward their state was rich and strong, with the ambition to trample the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Since Houjin's day the Turks had grown rich and strong, with designs on the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 朝廷既與之和親，歲給繒絮、錦彩十萬段。

translations.literal: Once the court had made peace through marriage, each year they gave one hundred thousand lengths of silk floss and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The court married into the house and paid one hundred thousand lengths of silk and brocade each year.

sentences.zh: 突厥在京師者，又待以優禮，衣錦食肉，常以千數。

translations.literal: Turks in the capital were also treated with exceptional courtesy—clothed in brocade, eating meat—often numbering in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Turks at the capital were feasted in brocade and meat, often by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 齊人懼其寇掠，亦傾府藏以給之。

translations.literal: The Qi, fearing their raids, also emptied their treasuries to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, fearing their raids, emptied their treasuries to buy them off too.

sentences.zh: 他缽彌復驕傲，仍令其徒屬曰：「但使我在南兩個兒孝順，何憂無物邪？」

translations.literal: Tabo grew ever more arrogant and told his followers: 'So long as my two sons in the south are filial, why worry about lacking goods?'
translations.idiomatic: Tabo grew ever prouder and told his followers: 'If my two southern sons stay dutiful, why should we lack for goods?'

sentences.zh: 齊有沙門惠琳，掠入突厥中，因謂他缽曰：「齊國強富，皆為有佛法。」

translations.literal: There was a Qi monk named Huilin, carried off into the Turks, who therefore said to Tabo: 'Qi is strong and rich—all because it has the Buddhist Law.'
translations.idiomatic: A Qi monk named Huilin, taken captive among the Turks, told Tabo: 'Qi is strong and rich because it has the Buddhist Law.'

sentences.zh: 遂說以因緣果報之理。

translations.literal: He then expounded the principle of karma and retribution.
translations.idiomatic: He preached karma and retribution.

sentences.zh: 他缽聞而信之，建一伽藍，遣使聘齊，求《淨名》、《涅槃》、《華嚴》等經，並《十誦律》。

translations.literal: Tabo heard and believed; he built a monastery, sent envoys to Qi, and sought the Vimalakirti, Nirvana, Avatamsaka, and other sutras, together with the Ten Recitations Vinaya.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo believed him, built a monastery, and sent to Qi for the Vimalakirti, Nirvana, Avatamsaka sutras and the Ten Recitations Vinaya.

sentences.zh: 他缽亦躬自齋戒，繞塔行道，恨不生內地。

translations.literal: Tabo also personally kept fasts, circled the stupa in walking meditation, and regretted that he was not born in the inner lands.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo himself fasted, circled the stupa in devotion, and lamented that he was not born in the civilized lands.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，他缽遣使獻馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande, Tabo sent envoys presenting horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year 2 Tabo sent horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 及齊滅，齊定州刺史、范陽王高紹義自馬邑奔之。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Qi's Dingzhou Inspector, Prince of Fanyang Gao Shaoyi, fled to him from Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, Prince of Fanyang Gao Shaoyi, Dingzhou inspector, fled to him from Mayi.

sentences.zh: 他缽立紹義為齊帝，召集所部，雲為之復仇。

translations.literal: Tabo installed Shaoyi as Emperor of Qi, gathered his tribes, and declared he would avenge him.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo made Shaoyi Emperor of Qi, rallied his tribes, and vowed revenge for him.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年四月，他缽遂入寇幽州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Xuanzheng, Tabo then invaded Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xuanzheng year 1 Tabo invaded Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 柱國劉雄拒戰，兵敗死之。

translations.literal: Pillar of State Liu Xiong resisted in battle; his army was defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of State Liu Xiong met him in battle, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總六軍，將北伐，會帝崩，乃班師。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu personally commanded the Six Armies and was about to campaign north; when the emperor died, the army was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu took the field to march north, but the emperor died and the army turned back.

sentences.zh: 是冬，他缽復寇邊，圍酒泉，大掠而去。

translations.literal: That winter Tabo again raided the frontier, besieged Jiuquan, plundered on a great scale, and left.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Tabo raided again, besieged Jiuquan, plundered heavily, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，他缽復請和親，帝策趙王招女為千金公主以嫁之，並遣執紹義送闕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, Tabo again requested marriage; the emperor designated the daughter of Prince Zhao Zhao as Princess Qianjin to marry him, and also sent to seize Shaoyi and deliver him to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang Tabo sought peace again; the emperor gave him Prince Zhao's daughter as Princess Qianjin and ordered Shaoyi seized and sent to court.

sentences.zh: 他缽不許，仍寇并州。

translations.literal: Tabo would not agree and again raided Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo refused and raided Bingzhou again.

sentences.zh: 二年，始遣使奉獻，且迎公主為親，而紹義尚留不遣。

translations.literal: In the second year he first sent envoys with tribute and to welcome the princess in marriage, but Shaoyi was still detained and not sent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he sent tribute and came for the princess, but still held Shaoyi back.

sentences.zh: 帝又令賀若誼往諭之，始送紹義。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent He Ruo Yi to instruct him, and only then was Shaoyi sent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent He Ruo Yi to reason with him, and only then did Tabo release Shaoyi.

sentences.zh: 他缽病且卒，謂其子庵邏曰：「吾聞親莫過於父子。

translations.literal: When Tabo fell ill and was near death, he said to his son Anluo: 'I have heard that no kinship surpasses father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo lay dying and told his son Anluo: 'I have heard that nothing binds like father and son.

sentences.zh: 吾兄不親其子，委位於我，我死，汝當避大邏便。」

translations.literal: My elder brother did not favor his own son but entrusted the throne to me; when I die, you should yield to Daluobian.'
translations.idiomatic: My brother passed over his son for me; when I die, you must yield to Daluobian.'

sentences.zh: 及卒，國中將立大邏便，以其母賤，眾不服。

translations.literal: When he died, the state was about to install Daluobian, but because his mother was lowborn the multitude would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the realm meant to install Daluobian, but his mother was of low birth and the people would not have it.

sentences.zh: 庵邏實貴，突厥素重之。

translations.literal: Anluo was truly noble; the Turks had always honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Anluo was of high birth and the Turks had long esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 攝圖最後至，謂國中曰：「若立庵邏者，我當率兄弟以事之；

translations.literal: Shetu arrived last and said to the state: 'If you install Anluo, I shall lead my brothers to serve him;
translations.idiomatic: Shetu came last and told the assembly: 'If you install Anluo, my brothers and I will serve him;

sentences.zh: 如立大邏便，我必守境，利刃長矛以相待。」

translations.literal: if you install Daluobian, I shall hold the frontier and meet you with sharp blades and long spears.'
translations.idiomatic: if you install Daluobian, I will hold the border and meet you with blade and spear.'

sentences.zh: 攝圖長而且雄，國人莫敢拒，竟立庵邏為嗣。

translations.literal: Shetu was tall and fierce; none in the state dared refuse him, and in the end Anluo was installed as successor.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu was tall and fierce; none dared oppose him, and Anluo was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 大邏便不得立，心不服庵邏，每遣人詈辱之。

translations.literal: Daluobian could not be installed; in his heart he did not submit to Anluo and often sent men to revile and humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: Daluobian was passed over; resenting Anluo, he sent men again and again to insult him.

sentences.zh: 庵邏不能制，因以國讓攝圖。

translations.literal: Anluo could not control him and therefore yielded the state to Shetu.
translations.idiomatic: Anluo could not restrain him and yielded the realm to Shetu.

sentences.zh: 國中相與議曰：「四可汗子，攝圖最賢。」

translations.literal: The state deliberated together, saying: 'Of the four qaghan's sons, Shetu is the most worthy.'
translations.idiomatic: The realm agreed: 'Of the four sons of the qaghan, Shetu is the ablest.'

sentences.zh: 因迎立之，號伊利俱盧設莫何始波羅可汗，一號沙缽略，居都斤山。

translations.literal: They therefore welcomed and installed him, with the title Yili Julu She Mohe Shiboluo Qaghan, also called Shaboluo, residing on Mount Dujin.
translations.idiomatic: They enthroned him as Yili Julu She Mohe Shiboluo Qaghan, also called Shaboluo, on Mount Dujin.

sentences.zh: 庵邏降居獨洛水，稱第三可汗。

translations.literal: Anluo descended to dwell on the Duluo River and styled himself the Third Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Anluo withdrew to the Duluo River as the Third Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 大邏便乃謂沙缽略曰：「我與爾俱可汗子，各承父後，爾今極尊，我獨無位，何也？」

translations.literal: Daluobian then said to Shaboluo: 'You and I are both sons of the qaghan, each inheriting after our father—yet you are now supreme while I alone have no rank. Why?'
translations.idiomatic: Daluobian said to Shaboluo: 'We are both sons of the qaghan, heirs after our father—yet you sit supreme while I have no place. Why?'

sentences.zh: 沙缽略患之，以為阿波可汗，還領所部。

translations.literal: Shaboluo was troubled by this and made him Apo Qaghan, returning him to lead his own division.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo, troubled, made him Apo Qaghan and sent him back to his own tribes.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略勇而得眾，北夷皆歸附之。

translations.literal: Shaboluo was brave and won the people; all the northern barbarians submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo was brave and won the people; the northern tribes all submitted.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，待之甚薄，北夷大怨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he treated them very sparingly; the northern barbarians were greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he treated them coldly and the northern tribes were deeply aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 會營州刺史高寶甯作亂，沙缽略與之合軍，攻陷臨渝鎮。

translations.literal: When Yingzhou Inspector Gao Baoning rebelled, Shaboluo joined forces with him and captured Linyu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzhou Inspector Gao Baoning rebelled, Shaboluo joined him and took Linyu garrison.

sentences.zh: 上敕緣邊修保鄣，峻長城，以備之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the frontier to repair protective walls and heighten the Long Wall to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the frontier to repair defenses and raise the Long Wall against them.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略妻，周千金公主，傷宗祀絕滅，由是悉眾來寇，控弦士四十萬。

translations.literal: Shaboluo's wife was Zhou's Princess Qianjin; grieving that her ancestral sacrifices were cut off, for this reason he led his entire host in invasion—four hundred thousand bowmen.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo's wife was Zhou's Princess Qianjin; mourning her fallen house, he marched in full force with four hundred thousand bowmen.

sentences.zh: 上令柱國馮昱屯乙弗泊，蘭州總管叱李崇屯幽州，達奚長儒據周槃，皆為虜敗。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Pillar of State Feng Yu to encamp at Yifu Marsh, Lanzhou Commander-in-Chief Chi Li Chong to encamp at Youzhou, and Daxi Changru to hold Zhoupan—all were defeated by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posted Feng Yu at Yifu Marsh, Chi Li Chong at Youzhou, and Daxi Changru at Zhoupan—all were beaten by the Turks.

sentences.zh: 於是縱兵自木硤、石門兩道來寇，武威、天水、安定、金城、上郡、弘化、延安六畜咸盡。

translations.literal: He then let his troops raid by the Muxia and Shimen routes; in Wuwei, Tianshui, Anding, Jincheng, Shangjun, Honghua, and Yan'an the six kinds of livestock were all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He swept in by the Muxia and Shimen routes and stripped Wuwei, Tianshui, Anding, Jincheng, Shangjun, Honghua, and Yan'an of all livestock.

sentences.zh: 天子震怒，下詔曰：

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was greatly angered and issued an edict, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 往者周、齊抗衡，分割諸夏，突厥之虜，俱通二國。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou and Qi contended on equal terms, dividing the lands of Xia; the Turkic barbarians communicated with both states alike.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou and Qi stood divided, each courting the Turks.

sentences.zh: 周人東慮，恐齊好之深；

translations.literal: The Zhou in the east worried, fearing Qi's intimacy with them was deep;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou in the east feared Qi's friendship with them;

sentences.zh: 齊氏西虞，懼周交之厚。

translations.literal: Qi in the west was anxious, fearing Zhou's ties with them were thick.
translations.idiomatic: Qi in the west feared Zhou's ties with them.

sentences.zh: 各謂慮意輕重，國遂安危。

translations.literal: Each judged the weight of the other's concern, and the state's safety or peril followed.
translations.idiomatic: Each judged the other's courtship by how much the rival feared it, and called that national safety or peril.

sentences.zh: 非徒並有大敵之憂，思減一邊之防。

translations.literal: It was not only that both had the worry of a great enemy; each also wished to reduce defense on one flank.
translations.idiomatic: They did not only fear a great enemy; each hoped to strip the other's frontier guard.

sentences.zh: 竭生靈之力，供其來往，傾府庫之財，棄於沙漠。

translations.literal: They exhausted the strength of the living to supply their comings and goings, emptied the treasuries, and cast wealth into the desert.
translations.idiomatic: They drained the people's strength to feed Turk envoys and poured treasury gold into the desert.

sentences.zh: 華夏之地，實為勞擾。

translations.literal: The lands of Huaxia were truly worn and troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains were worn to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 朕受天明命，子育萬方，湣臣下之勞，除既往之弊。

translations.literal: I have received Heaven's clear mandate and nurture the myriad regions; I pity my ministers' toil and remove past abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gave me the mandate to nurture all lands; I pity my servants' toil and end these old abuses.

sentences.zh: 回入賊之物，加賜將士；

translations.literal: Goods taken back from the enemy are added as rewards for officers and soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: What we recover from the enemy goes to our soldiers;

sentences.zh: 息在路之人，務於耕織。

translations.literal: those on the roads are given rest and urged to plow and weave.
translations.idiomatic: travelers on the roads are spared so they may farm and weave.

sentences.zh: 凶醜愚暗，未知深旨，將大定之日，比戰國之時，乘昔世之驕，結今時之恨。

translations.literal: The vicious and ugly, stupid and dark, do not know the deep intent; on the eve of great pacification they compare it to the Warring States era, riding the pride of former ages to forge present hatred.
translations.idiomatic: The brutish Turks, dull and blind to my intent, treat this age of unification like the Warring States, nursing old pride into new hatred.

sentences.zh: 近者，盡其巢窟，俱犯北邊，而遠鎮偏師，逢而摧翦，未及南上，遽已奔北。

translations.literal: Recently they emptied their nests and all invaded the northern border; yet distant garrisons and detached columns met and cut them down—before they could march south they had already fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Lately they poured from their nests against the north, but our distant garrisons met and shattered them before they could march south—they fled north at once.

sentences.zh: 且彼渠師，其數凡五，昆季爭長，父叔相猜，世行暴虐，家法殘忍。

translations.literal: Moreover their chieftains number five in all; brothers contend for supremacy, fathers and uncles suspect one another; generation after generation they practice cruelty, and their household law is savage.
translations.idiomatic: Their chiefs number five; brothers vie for power, fathers and uncles mistrust one another; cruelty is their custom and savagery their house law.

sentences.zh: 東夷諸國，盡挾私讎；

translations.literal: The eastern Yi states all harbor private grudges;
translations.idiomatic: The eastern tribes all nurse private grudges;

sentences.zh: 西戎群長，皆有宿怨。

translations.literal: the western Rong chieftains all have old enmities.
translations.idiomatic: the western chiefs all bear old enmities.

sentences.zh: 突厥之北，契骨之徒，切齒磨牙，常伺其後。

translations.literal: North of the Turks, the Qigu and their kind gnash teeth and grind jaws, ever watching for their rear.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Turks, the Qigu gnash their teeth and watch for their moment.

sentences.zh: 達頭前攻酒泉，于闐、波斯、揖怛三國，一時即叛；

translations.literal: Datou earlier attacked Jiuquan; Khotan, Persia, and the Yeda states rebelled at once;
translations.idiomatic: Datou attacked Jiuquan; Khotan, Persia, and Yeda rebelled at once;

sentences.zh: 沙缽略近趣周槃，其部內薄孤、東紇羅尋亦翻動。

translations.literal: Shaboluo recently pressed toward Zhoupan; within his division Bogu and Dong Heluo also stirred in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo lately pressed Zhoupan; within his ranks Bogu and Dong Heluo rose against him.

sentences.zh: 往年利稽察大為高麗、靺鞨所破，沙毗設又為紇支可汗所殺。

translations.literal: In former years Lijicha was greatly broken by Koguryo and Mohe; Shabi She was again killed by Hezhi Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Lijicha was shattered by Koguryo and Mohe; Shabi She was slain by Hezhi Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 與其為鄰，皆願誅剿，部落之下，盡異純人。

translations.literal: All who border them wish to exterminate them; beneath the tribes none are of pure Turk stock.
translations.idiomatic: Every neighbor wishes them destroyed; beneath the tribes no man is of pure Turk blood.

sentences.zh: 千種萬類，仇敵怨偶，泣血拊心，銜悲積恨。

translations.literal: Thousands of kinds and myriad sorts—enemies and resentful mates—weep blood and beat their breasts, bearing grief and heaping hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of peoples—foes and bitter kin—weep blood, beat their breasts, and heap hatred upon hatred.

sentences.zh: 圓首方足，皆人類也，有一於此，更切朕懷。

translations.literal: Round heads and square feet—all are human kind; that any should suffer thus cuts deeper into my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Round heads on square feet—they are human too; that any should suffer so cuts me to the heart.

sentences.zh: 彼地咎征妖作，將年一紀。

translations.literal: In their lands ominous signs and demonic portents have appeared for nearly a full cycle of years.
translations.idiomatic: In their lands omens and portents have stalked them for nearly twelve years.

sentences.zh: 乃獸為人語，人作神言，雲其國亡，訖而不見。

translations.literal: Beasts spoke with human voices, men uttered divine words, saying their state would perish—yet it has not yet been seen.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts spoke like men, men like gods, prophesying their fall—yet they still stand.

sentences.zh: 每冬雷震，觸地火生。

translations.literal: Every winter thunder rolls and fire springs from the ground where struck.
translations.idiomatic: Every winter thunder rolls and fire bursts from the earth.

sentences.zh: 種類資給，唯藉水草，去歲四時，竟無雨雪，川枯蝗暴，卉木燒盡，饑疫死亡，人畜相半。

translations.literal: Their people's sustenance depends solely on grass and water; last year through all four seasons there was no rain or snow; rivers dried, locusts swarmed, plants and trees burned away; famine and pestilence brought death—men and livestock halved.
translations.idiomatic: They live on grass and water alone; last year through four seasons came no rain or snow; rivers dried, locusts swarmed, the steppe burned; famine and plague halved men and beasts.

sentences.zh: 舊居之地，赤土無依，遷徙漠南，偷存晷刻。

translations.literal: Their old dwelling places are bare red earth without support; they have migrated south of the desert, stealing survival by the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Their old pastures are bare red earth; they have fled south of the desert, clinging to life by the hour.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋上天所忿，驅就齊斧，幽明合契，今也其時。

translations.literal: This is surely Heaven's wrath, driving them toward the executioner's axe; dark and bright align in accord—now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven itself is angry, driving them to the axe; dark and bright align—now is the hour.

sentences.zh: 故選將練兵，贏糧聚甲，義士奮發，壯夫肆憤，願取名王之首，思撻單于之背。

translations.literal: Therefore I select generals and drill soldiers, pack grain and gather armor; men of righteousness rise in zeal, stalwarts unleash their wrath, wishing to take the heads of famous kings and longing to flog the shanyu's back.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I choose generals, drill troops, pack grain and gather armor; righteous men rise, stalwarts burn to take famous heads and lash the shanyu's back.

sentences.zh: 此則王恢所說，其猶射癰，何敵能當，何遠不克。

translations.literal: This is what Wang Hui spoke of—it is like shooting an abscess; what enemy could withstand it, what distance could not be conquered?
translations.idiomatic: This is Wang Hui's counsel—like lancing an abscess; no foe could stand, no land lay beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 但皇王舊跡，北止幽都，荒遐之表，文軌所棄，得其地不可而居，得其人不忍皆殺。

translations.literal: But the ancient track of emperors and kings extends north only to Youdu; beyond the wild and remote reaches lies territory abandoned by culture and law—gaining the land one cannot dwell in it, gaining the people one cannot bear to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ancient bounds of empire reach north only to Youdu; beyond the wild frontier lies land that civilization has forsaken—take the territory and you cannot hold it; take the people and you cannot slaughter them all.

sentences.zh: 無勞兵革，遠規溟海。

translations.literal: There is no need to weary oneself with arms and armor, scheming far toward the distant sea.
translations.idiomatic: Let us not exhaust ourselves with war, scheming as far as the distant sea.

sentences.zh: 普告海內，知朕意焉。

translations.literal: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm, that all may know my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm, that all may know my mind.

sentences.zh: 於是河間王弘、上柱國豆盧績、竇榮定、左僕射高熲、右僕射虞慶則並為元帥，出塞擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Hong of Hejian, Upper Pillar of State Dou Lu Ji, Dou Rongding, Left Vice Director Gao Yong, and Right Vice Director Yu Qingze were all made commanders-in-chief and marched beyond the frontier to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Prince Hong of Hejian, Dou Lu Ji, Dou Rongding, Gao Yong, and Yu Qingze were all appointed supreme commanders and marched beyond the frontier to strike them.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略率阿波、貪汗二可汗來拒戰，皆敗走。

translations.literal: Shaboluo led the two qaghans Apo and Tanhan to meet them in battle; all were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo led the qaghans Apo and Tanhan to meet them in battle; all were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 時虜饑不能得食，粉骨為糧，又多災疫，死者極眾。

translations.literal: At the time the barbarians were starving and could obtain no food; they ground bone into provisions, and pestilence was widespread besides—the dead were exceedingly many.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians were starving, grinding bone into food; pestilence swept them as well, and the dead were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 既而沙缽略以阿波驍悍，忌之，因其先歸，襲擊其部，大破之，殺阿波母。

translations.literal: Before long Shaboluo, because Apo was fierce and bold, envied him; taking advantage of his having returned first, he attacked Apo's division, routed it utterly, and killed Apo's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shaboluo, envying Apo's fierceness, struck while Apo was still returning home, crushing his division and killing Apo's mother.

sentences.zh: 阿波還無所歸，西奔達頭可汗。

translations.literal: Apo returned with nowhere to go and fled west to Qaghan Datou.
translations.idiomatic: Apo returned to find nowhere to go and fled west to Datou Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 達頭者，名玷厥，沙缽略之從父也，舊為西面可汗。

translations.literal: Datou, personal name Dianjue, was Shaboluo's uncle by the father's side; he had formerly been Qaghan of the Western Sector.
translations.idiomatic: Datou, whose personal name was Dianjue, was Shaboluo's paternal uncle and had formerly been Qaghan of the Western Sector.

sentences.zh: 既而大怒，遣阿波率兵而東，其部落歸之者將十萬騎，遂與沙缽略相攻。

translations.literal: He then flew into a great rage and sent Apo east at the head of troops; tribes rallying to him numbered nearly one hundred thousand horsemen, and they thereupon fought Shaboluo.
translations.idiomatic: He flew into a rage and sent Apo east with an army; nearly a hundred thousand horsemen rallied to them, and they turned to fight Shaboluo.

sentences.zh: 又有貪汗可汗，素睦于阿波，沙缽略奪其眾而廢之，貪汗亡奔達頭。

translations.literal: There was also Qaghan Tanhan, who had long been on good terms with Apo; Shaboluo seized his following and deposed him, and Tanhan fled in exile to Datou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Tanhan Qaghan, long friendly with Apo; Shaboluo seized his people and deposed him, and Tanhan fled to Datou.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略從弟地勤察，別統部落，與沙缽略有隙，復以眾叛歸阿波。

translations.literal: Shaboluo's younger cousin Diqincha, who separately commanded a tribal division, had a rift with Shaboluo and again led his people in rebellion to join Apo.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo's cousin Diqincha, who commanded a separate division, had fallen out with him and again led his tribes in revolt to Apo.

sentences.zh: 連兵不已，各遣使詣闕，請和求援，上皆不許。

translations.literal: They fought without cease; each sent envoys to the imperial court seeking peace and aid, but the emperor refused all.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting continued without end; each side sent envoys to court seeking peace and aid, but the emperor refused them all.

sentences.zh: 會千金公主上書，請為一子之例，文帝遣開府徐平和使于沙缽略。

translations.literal: When Princess Qianjin memorialized the throne, asking that they be treated as father and son, Emperor Wen sent Palace Gate Commissioner Xu Ping as envoy to Shaboluo.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Qianjin then memorialized the throne, asking that they be treated as father and son; Emperor Wen sent Palace Gate Commissioner Xu Ping as envoy to Shaboluo.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣時鎮并州，請因其釁乘之，上不許。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang was then administering Bingzhou; he asked to seize the opportunity of their strife to strike, but the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yang Guang was then stationed at Bingzhou and asked to exploit their strife with an attack, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略遣使致書曰：「辰年九月十日，從天生大突厥天下賢聖天子伊利俱盧設莫何始波羅可汗致書大隋皇帝：使人開府徐平和至，辱告言語，具聞也。

translations.literal: Shaboluo sent an envoy with a letter, saying: 'On the tenth day of the ninth month of the chen year, Yili Julu She Mohe Shiboluo Qaghan, sage and holy Son of Heaven of the great Turks born from Heaven, addresses the Emperor of Great Sui: Commissioner of the Palace Gate Xu Ping has arrived; I am honored by your message and have heard it all.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo sent an envoy with a letter: 'On the tenth day of the ninth month of the chen year, Yili Julu She Mohe Shiboluo Qaghan, sage Son of Heaven of the great Turks born from Heaven, writes to the Emperor of Great Sui: your envoy Xu Ping has arrived; I am honored by your words and have heard them all.

sentences.zh: 皇帝是婦父，即是翁，此是女夫，即是兒例，兩境雖殊，情義是一。

translations.literal: The Emperor is my wife's father—that is to say, my father-in-law; I am the Emperor's daughter's husband—that is to say, his son by custom; though our two realms differ, our bond of feeling is one.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor is my wife's father—that is, my father-in-law; I am his daughter's husband—that is, his son by custom; though our realms differ, our bond is one.

sentences.zh: 今重疊親舊，子子孫孫，乃至萬世不斷。

translations.literal: Now our kinship is renewed again—sons and sons' sons, down to ten thousand generations without break.
translations.idiomatic: Now our kinship is renewed—sons and sons' sons, for ten thousand generations without end.

sentences.zh: 上天為證，終不違負。

translations.literal: Heaven be witness—I shall never betray this pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven be witness—I shall never break this pledge.

sentences.zh: 此國所有羊、馬，都是皇帝畜生；

translations.literal: All the sheep and horses of this land are the Emperor's livestock;
translations.idiomatic: All the sheep and horses of this land belong to the Emperor;

sentences.zh: 彼有繒彩，都是此物。

translations.literal: the silk and brocades there are all likewise his goods.
translations.idiomatic: the silks and brocades there are all his goods as well.

sentences.zh: 彼此不異也。」

translations.literal: Between us there is no difference.'
translations.idiomatic: Between us there is no difference at all.'

sentences.zh: 文帝報書曰：「大隋天子貽書大突厥伊利俱盧設莫何沙缽略可汗：得書，知大有好心向此也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen replied in a letter: 'The Son of Heaven of Great Sui sends this letter to Yili Julu She Mohe Shaboluo Qaghan of the great Turks: having received your letter, I know you harbor great goodwill toward us.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen replied: 'The Son of Heaven of Great Sui sends this letter to Yili Julu She Mohe Shaboluo Qaghan of the great Turks: I have your letter and know you bear great goodwill toward us.

sentences.zh: 既是沙缽略婦翁，今日看沙缽略共兒子不異。

translations.literal: Since I am Shaboluo's father-in-law, today I regard Shaboluo as no different from a son.
translations.idiomatic: As Shaboluo's father-in-law, I now regard him as no different from a son.

sentences.zh: 既以親舊厚意，常使之外，今特別遣大臣虞慶則往彼看女，復看沙缽略也。」

translations.literal: Out of the deep goodwill of kinship I have always sent envoys; now I especially dispatch the great minister Yu Qingze to go there to see my daughter, and to see Shaboluo as well.'
translations.idiomatic: Out of the goodwill of kinship I have always sent envoys; now I especially send the great minister Yu Qingze to see my daughter there, and to see Shaboluo as well.'

sentences.zh: 沙缽略陳兵列其寶物，坐見慶則，稱病不能起，且曰：「我伯父以來，不向人拜。」

translations.literal: Shaboluo arrayed his troops and displayed his treasures, and received Yu Qingze seated; he claimed illness and could not rise, and said: 'Since my uncle's time, we have not bowed to anyone.'
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo drew up his troops, displayed his treasures, and received Yu Qingze seated; pleading illness, he would not rise, and said: 'Since my uncle's day we have bowed to no one.'

sentences.zh: 慶則責而喻之。

translations.literal: Yu Qingze rebuked him and instructed him with reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qingze rebuked him and reasoned with him.

sentences.zh: 千金公主私謂慶則曰：「可汗豺狼性，過與爭，將齧人。」

translations.literal: Princess Qianjin privately told Yu Qingze: 'The qaghan has a wolf's nature; press him too hard and he will bite.'
translations.idiomatic: Princess Qianjin privately told Yu Qingze: 'The qaghan has a wolf's nature; press him too hard and he will bite.'

sentences.zh: 長孫晟說諭之，攝圖屈，乃頓顙受璽書，以戴於首。

translations.literal: Chang Sun Sheng persuaded and instructed him; Shetu yielded, then bowed his forehead to the ground to receive the imperial letter and placed it on his head.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Sun Sheng persuaded him; Shetu yielded, bowed his forehead to the ground to receive the imperial letter, and placed it on his head.

sentences.zh: 既而大慚，其群下因相聚慟哭。

translations.literal: Afterward he was deeply ashamed, and his followers gathered together and wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was deeply ashamed, and his followers gathered and wept together.

sentences.zh: 慶則又遣稱臣，沙缽略謂其屬曰：「何名為臣？」

translations.literal: Yu Qingze also had him styled as subject; Shaboluo said to his followers: 'What is meant by "subject"?'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qingze also had him styled as subject; Shaboluo asked his followers: 'What does "subject" mean?'

sentences.zh: 報曰：「隋國臣，猶此稱奴。」

translations.literal: They replied: 'A subject of Sui—here it is like calling oneself a servant.'
translations.idiomatic: They replied: 'A subject of Sui—in our terms, it is like calling oneself a servant.'

sentences.zh: 沙缽略曰：「得作大隋天子奴，虞僕射之力也。」

translations.literal: Shaboluo said: 'That I may become a servant of the Son of Heaven of Great Sui is owing to Vice Director Yu's power.'
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo said: 'That I may become a servant of the Son of Heaven of Great Sui is Vice Director Yu's doing.'

sentences.zh: 贈慶則馬千匹，並以從妹妻之。

translations.literal: He presented Yu Qingze with a thousand horses and gave him a younger female cousin in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Yu Qingze a thousand horses and married him to a younger female cousin.

sentences.zh: 時沙缽略既為達頭所困，又東畏契丹，遣使告急，請將部落度漠南，寄居白道川內。

translations.literal: At the time Shaboluo was already hard pressed by Datou and also feared the Khitan to the east; he sent envoys in urgent appeal, asking to lead his tribes south across the desert to lodge within the White Road River valley.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo was already hard pressed by Datou and feared the Khitan to the east; he sent envoys in urgent appeal, asking to lead his tribes south across the desert to settle within the White Road River valley.

sentences.zh: 有詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣以兵援之，給以衣食，賜以車服、鼓吹。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang came to his aid with troops, supplied food and clothing, and granted carriage trappings and musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yang Guang came to his aid with troops, supplied food and clothing, and granted carriages, robes, and musicians.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略因西擊阿波，破擒之。

translations.literal: Shaboluo then marched west against Apo, defeated him, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo then marched west against Apo, defeated him, and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 而阿拔國部落乘虛掠其妻子。

translations.literal: But the Abakuo tribe seized the moment to raid and carry off his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: But the Abakuo tribe seized the moment and carried off his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 官軍為擊阿拔，敗之，所獲悉與沙缽略。

translations.literal: The imperial army attacked Abakuo in his stead, defeated them, and gave all that was taken wholly to Shaboluo.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army attacked Abakuo on his behalf, defeated them, and gave all that was recovered to Shaboluo.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略大喜，乃立約，以磧為界。

translations.literal: Shaboluo rejoiced greatly and thereupon made a covenant setting the desert sands as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo rejoiced greatly and made a covenant with the desert sands as the boundary.

sentences.zh: 因上表曰：「大突厥伊利俱盧設始波羅莫何可汗臣攝圖言：大使、尚書右僕射虞慶則至，伏奉詔書，兼宣慈旨，仰惟恩信之著，愈久愈明，徒知負荷，不能答謝。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial, saying: 'Your subject Shetu, Qaghan of the great Turks Yili Julu She Shiboluo Mohe, reports: the grand envoy, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Qingze has arrived; I humbly received the imperial edict and heard also your gracious intent. Reflecting on how your favor and trust grow ever clearer with time, I can only feel the burden and know not how to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial: 'Your subject Shetu, Qaghan of the great Turks Yili Julu She Shiboluo Mohe, reports: the grand envoy, Right Vice Director Yu Qingze has arrived; I humbly received the imperial edict and your gracious message. Your favor and trust grow clearer with time; I feel only the burden and know not how to repay it.

sentences.zh: 突厥自天置以來，五十餘載，保有沙漠，自王蕃隅，地過萬里，士馬億數，恆力兼戎夷，抗禮華夏，在於戎狄，莫與為大。

translations.literal: Since Heaven established the Turks, more than fifty years have passed; we held the desert sands, ourselves kings of the borderlands; our lands extend more than ten thousand li, our warriors and horses number in the hundreds of millions; we constantly matched strength against the Rong and the Yi and claimed parity with Huaxia—among the barbarians, none was our equal.
translations.idiomatic: Since Heaven established the Turks more than fifty years ago, we have held the desert and ruled the borderlands; our lands stretch ten thousand li, our warriors and horses beyond count; we matched strength with the Rong and Yi and claimed parity with Huaxia—among the barbarians, none was our equal.

sentences.zh: 頃者，氣候清和，風雪順序，意以華夏其有大聖興焉。

translations.literal: Of late the seasons have been clear and mild, wind and snow have followed their proper order—we took it that a great sage was rising in Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: Of late the seasons have been clear and mild, wind and snow in their proper order—we took it that a great sage was rising in Huaxia.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大隋皇帝真皇帝也，豈敢阻兵恃險，偷竊名號？

translations.literal: We reflect that the Emperor of Great Sui is a true emperor—how would we dare block the way with arms, rely on perilous terrain, and steal a title for ourselves?
translations.idiomatic: We reflect that the Emperor of Great Sui is a true emperor—how would we dare block the way with arms, rely on perilous terrain, and steal a title?

sentences.zh: 今便感慕淳風，歸心有道。

translations.literal: Now we are moved by your pure customs and turn our hearts to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Now we are moved by your pure customs and turn our hearts to the Way.

sentences.zh: 雖復南瞻魏闕，山川悠遠，北面之禮不敢廢。

translations.literal: Though we gaze south toward the Wei towers across distant mountains and rivers, we dare not abandon the rites due toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: Though we gaze south toward the imperial towers across distant mountains and rivers, we dare not abandon the rites of facing north.

sentences.zh: 當令侍子入朝，神馬歲貢，朝夕恭承，惟命是親。

translations.literal: We shall send a hostage son to court, tribute horses each year; morning and evening we shall respectfully obey—your will is our command.
translations.idiomatic: We shall send a hostage son to court and tribute horses each year; morning and evening we shall obey—your will is our command.

sentences.zh: 謹遣第七兒臣窟合真等奉表以聞。」

translations.literal: Respectfully we send my seventh son, your subject Kutu Hezhen, and others to present this memorial for your hearing.'
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully I send my seventh son, your subject Kutu Hezhen, and others to present this memorial.'

sentences.zh: 文帝下詔曰：「沙缽略往雖與和，猶是二國，今作君臣，便成一體。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen issued an edict: 'Though Shaboluo and we made peace before, we were still two states; now as lord and subject we become one whole.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen issued an edict: 'Though Shaboluo and we made peace before, we were still two states; now as lord and subject we are one whole.

sentences.zh: 已敕有司，肅告郊廟，宜傳播天下，咸使知聞。」

translations.literal: I have charged the relevant offices to solemnly announce this at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; let it be spread throughout the realm so that all may know.'
translations.idiomatic: I have charged the relevant offices to announce this solemnly at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; let it be spread throughout the realm so that all may know.'

sentences.zh: 自是詔答諸事，並不稱其名以異之。

translations.literal: Henceforth in edicts and replies on all matters his personal name was not used, to mark him apart with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth in edicts and replies on all matters his personal name was not used, to honor him apart.

sentences.zh: 其妻可賀敦周千金公主，賜姓楊氏，編之屬籍，改封大義公主。

translations.literal: His wife, Khatun, Zhou's Princess Qianjin, was granted the surname Yang, entered into the imperial register, and was re-enfeoffed as Princess Dayi.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Khatun, Zhou's Princess Qianjin, was granted the surname Yang, entered into the imperial register, and re-enfeoffed as Princess Dayi.

sentences.zh: 策拜窟合真為柱國，封安國公，宴於內殿，引見皇后，賞勞甚厚。

translations.literal: By imperial decree Kutu Hezhen was appointed Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Anguo; he was feasted in the inner hall and introduced to the empress; rewards and honors were exceedingly generous.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial decree Kutu Hezhen was appointed Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Anguo; he was feasted in the inner hall, introduced to the empress, and rewarded most generously.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略大悅。

translations.literal: Shaboluo was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 於是，歲時貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute at the seasons never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter seasonal tribute never ceased.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，沙缽略遣其子入貢方物。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, Shaboluo sent his son to present tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, Shaboluo sent his son to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 因請獵於恆、代之間，詔許之，仍遣使人，賜其酒食。

translations.literal: He also asked to hunt between Heng and Dai; an edict permitted it, and envoys were furthermore sent to grant him wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to hunt between Heng and Dai; an edict permitted it, and envoys were sent with wine and food.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略率部落再拜受賜。

translations.literal: Shaboluo led his tribes in double obeisance to receive the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo led his tribes in double obeisance to receive the gifts.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略一日手殺鹿十八頭，齎尾舌以獻。

translations.literal: In one day Shaboluo personally killed eighteen deer and brought tails and tongues as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In one day Shaboluo personally killed eighteen deer and brought tails and tongues as tribute.

sentences.zh: 還至紫河鎮，其牙帳為火所燒，沙缽略惡之，月餘而卒。

translations.literal: Returning to Zihe garrison, his royal tent was burned by fire; Shaboluo took this as a bad omen and died a little over a month later.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Zihe garrison, his royal tent was burned by fire; Shaboluo took it as an ill omen and died a little over a month later.

sentences.zh: 上為之廢朝三日，遣太常弔祭焉，贈物五千段。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court for three days on his account, sent the Minister of Rites to offer condolences and sacrifices, and granted five thousand bolts of goods.
