translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court for three days on his account, sent the Minister of Rites to offer condolences and sacrifices, and granted five thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 初，攝圖以其子雍虞閭性懦，遣令立其弟葉護處羅侯。

translations.literal: At first Shetu, because his son Yongyulü was timid by nature, ordered that his younger brother Yehu Chuluo be installed instead.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shetu, finding his son Yongyulü timid by nature, ordered that his younger brother Yehu Chuluo be installed instead.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭遣使迎處羅侯，將立之，處羅侯曰：「我突厥自木杆可汗來，多以弟代兄，以庶奪嫡，失先祖之法，不相敬畏。

translations.literal: Yongyulü sent envoys to welcome Chuluo and was about to install him; Chuluo said: 'Among us Turks since Qaghan Mugan, younger brothers have often replaced elder brothers, inferior sons have seized the rightful heir's place—we have lost our ancestors' law and no longer fear and respect one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyulü sent envoys to welcome Chuluo and was about to install him; Chuluo said: 'Among us Turks since Qaghan Mugan, younger brothers have often replaced elder brothers and inferior sons have seized the rightful heir's place—we have lost our ancestors' law and no longer fear and respect one another.

sentences.zh: 汝當嗣位，我不憚拜汝也。」

translations.literal: You should succeed to the throne; I do not shrink from bowing to you.'
translations.idiomatic: You should succeed to the throne; I do not shrink from bowing to you.'

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭又遣使謂處羅侯曰：「叔與我父，共根連體，我是枝葉，寧有我作主，令根本反同枝葉？

translations.literal: Yongyulü again sent envoys telling Chuluo: 'Uncle and my father share one root and one body—I am the branch and leaf; how could I take the chieftainship and make the root become like the branch and leaf?
translations.idiomatic: Yongyulü again sent envoys telling Chuluo: 'Uncle and my father share one root and one body—I am the branch and leaf; how could I take the chieftainship and make the root become like the branch and leaf?

sentences.zh: 願叔勿疑。」

translations.literal: I beg you, uncle, do not doubt me.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, uncle, do not doubt me.'

sentences.zh: 相讓者五六，處羅侯竟立，是為葉護。

translations.literal: They yielded to one another five or six times; in the end Chuluo took the throne—this was Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: They yielded to one another five or six times; in the end Chuluo took the throne—this was Yehu.

sentences.zh: 遣使上表言狀，上賜之鼓吹、幡旗。

translations.literal: He sent envoys with a memorial reporting the situation; the emperor granted him musicians and banners.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys with a memorial reporting the situation; the emperor granted him musicians and banners.

sentences.zh: 處羅侯長頤僂背，眉目疏朗，勇而有謀。

translations.literal: Chuluo had a long face and a curved back; his brows and eyes were clear and open; he was brave and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo had a long face and a curved back, clear brows and eyes, and was brave and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 以隋所賜旗鼓，西征阿波，敵人以為得隋兵所助，多來降附，遂擒阿波。

translations.literal: With the drums and banners gifted by Sui he marched west against Apo; enemies thought he had gained aid from Sui troops, and many came to surrender; he thereupon captured Apo.
translations.idiomatic: With the drums and banners Sui had granted him he marched west against Apo; enemies thought he had Sui troops at his back, and many surrendered; he captured Apo.

sentences.zh: 既而上書，請阿波死生之命。

translations.literal: He then sent up a memorial asking the emperor to decide Apo's life or death.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent up a memorial asking the emperor to decide Apo's life or death.

sentences.zh: 上下其議，左僕射高熲進曰：「骨肉相殘，教之蠹也，宜存養以示寬大。」

translations.literal: The matter was deliberated at court; Left Vice Director Gao Yong advanced: 'Fratricide is a canker upon instruction; we should spare him and show magnanimity.'
translations.idiomatic: The matter was deliberated at court; Left Vice Director Gao Yong advanced: 'Fratricide is a canker upon instruction; we should spare him and show magnanimity.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Well said.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Well said.'

sentences.zh: 熲因奉觴進曰：「自軒轅以來，獯粥多為邊患。

translations.literal: Gao Yong then raised his cup and advanced: 'Since the time of the Yellow Emperor, the Xiongnu have often been a frontier scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yong then raised his cup and advanced: 'Since the time of the Yellow Emperor, the Xiongnu have often been a frontier scourge.

sentences.zh: 今遠窮北海，皆為臣妾，此之盛事，振古未聞。

translations.literal: Now they are driven to the far reaches of the Northern Sea and all have become subjects—such a triumph has never been heard of since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Now they are driven to the far reaches of the Northern Sea and all have become subjects—such a triumph has never been heard of since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臣敢再拜上壽。」

translations.literal: Your subject dares bow twice and offer a toast to your longevity.'
translations.idiomatic: Your subject dares bow twice and offer a toast to your longevity.'

sentences.zh: 後處羅侯又西征，中流矢卒，其眾奉雍虞閭為主，是為頡伽施多那都藍可汗。

translations.literal: Later Chuluo marched west again, was struck by an arrow midstream and died; his followers installed Yongyulü as their lord—this was Qaghan Jiegan Shinuodadu Dulan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chuluo marched west again, was struck by an arrow and died; his followers installed Yongyulü as their lord—this was Qaghan Jiegan Shinuodadu Dulan.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭遣使詣闕，賜物三千段，每歲遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Yongyulü sent envoys to the imperial court; he was granted three thousand bolts of goods and dispatched tribute envoys each year.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyulü sent envoys to court; he was granted three thousand bolts of goods and sent tribute envoys each year.

sentences.zh: 時有流人楊欽，亡入突厥中，謬雲彭國公劉昶與宇文氏謀反，令大義公主發兵擾邊。

translations.literal: At the time there was an exile, Yang Qin, who fled into the Turks and falsely claimed that Liu Chang, Duke of Peng, was plotting rebellion with the Yuwen clan, and that Princess Dayi should send troops to harass the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an exile, Yang Qin, fled into the Turks and falsely claimed that Liu Chang, Duke of Peng, was plotting rebellion with the Yuwen clan and that Princess Dayi should send troops to harass the frontier.

sentences.zh: 都藍執欽以聞，並貢勃布、魚膠。

translations.literal: Dulan seized Yang Qin and reported this, and also presented felt cloth and fish glue as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Dulan seized Yang Qin and reported this, and also presented felt cloth and fish glue as tribute.

sentences.zh: 其弟欽羽設部落強盛，都藍忌而擊之，斬首於陣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qinyushe's tribe was powerful; Dulan envied him and attacked, beheading him in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qinyushe's tribe was powerful; Dulan envied him, attacked, and beheaded him in battle.

sentences.zh: 其年，遣其母弟褥但特勤獻于闐玉杖，上拜褥但為柱國、康國公。

translations.literal: That year he sent his maternal younger brother Rudan Tegin to present a Khotan jade staff; the emperor appointed Rudan Grand Preceptor and Duke of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: That year he sent his maternal younger brother Rudan Tegin to present a Khotan jade staff; the emperor appointed Rudan Grand Preceptor and Duke of Kang.

sentences.zh: 明年，突厥部落大人相率遣使貢馬萬匹，羊二萬口，駝、牛各五百頭。

translations.literal: The next year the great leaders of the Turk tribes together dispatched envoys presenting ten thousand horses, twenty thousand sheep, and five hundred camels and cattle each.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the great leaders of the Turk tribes together sent envoys presenting ten thousand horses, twenty thousand sheep, and five hundred camels and cattle each.

sentences.zh: 尋遣請緣邊置市，與中國貿易，詔許之。

translations.literal: Soon they sent a request to establish border markets for trade with China; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they requested border markets for trade with China; an edict permitted it.

sentences.zh: 平陳後，上以陳叔寶屏風賜大義公主，主心恆不平，因書屏風為詩，敘陳亡以自寄曰：「盛衰等朝暮，世道若浮萍，榮華實難守，池台終自平。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Chen, the emperor gave Princess Dayi a painted screen of Chen Shubao; the princess's heart was always uneasy, and she wrote a poem on the screen, narrating Chen's fall to express her feelings, saying: 'Rise and fall are like dawn and dusk; the age is like duckweed on the water; glory and splendor are hard indeed to keep; pools and terraces in the end level themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Chen, the emperor gave Princess Dayi a painted screen of Chen Shubao; her heart was always uneasy, and she wrote a poem on the screen about Chen's fall, saying: 'Rise and fall are like dawn and dusk; the age is like duckweed on the water; glory is hard to keep; pools and terraces in the end level themselves.

sentences.zh: 富貴今安在？

translations.literal: Where is wealth and honor now?
translations.idiomatic: Where is wealth and honor now?

sentences.zh: 空事寫丹青。

translations.literal: Only vain figures remain painted on silk.
translations.idiomatic: Only vain figures remain painted on silk.

sentences.zh: 杯酒恆無樂，弦歌詎有聲？

translations.literal: Cups of wine bring no joy; can strings and songs still sound?
translations.idiomatic: Cups of wine bring no joy; can strings and songs still sound?

sentences.zh: 餘本皇家子，飄流入虜庭，一朝睹成敗，懷抱忽縱橫。

translations.literal: I was born a child of the imperial house, drifted as a refugee into the barbarians' court; one day seeing triumph and ruin, my breast suddenly overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: I was born a child of the imperial house, drifted as a refugee into the barbarians' court; one day seeing triumph and ruin, my breast suddenly overflowed.

sentences.zh: 古來共如此，非我獨申名。

translations.literal: Since olden times all have been thus—it is not I alone who speak this name.
translations.idiomatic: Since olden times all have been thus—it is not I alone who speak this name.

sentences.zh: 唯有《昭君曲》，偏傷遠嫁情。」

translations.literal: Only the "Song of Zhaojun" especially wounds the feeling of a distant marriage.'
translations.idiomatic: Only the "Song of Zhaojun" especially wounds the feeling of a distant marriage.'

sentences.zh: 上聞惡之，禮賜益薄。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this he took it ill; ceremonial gifts grew ever thinner.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he took it ill; ceremonial gifts grew ever thinner.

sentences.zh: 公主復與西突厥泥利可汗連結，上恐其為變，將圖之。

translations.literal: The princess again linked herself with Nili Qaghan of the Western Turks; the emperor feared she might stir trouble and planned against her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess again linked herself with Nili Qaghan of the Western Turks; the emperor feared she might stir trouble and planned against her.

sentences.zh: 會主與所從胡私通，因發其事，下詔廢之。

translations.literal: It happened that the princess had a private liaison with a Turk follower of hers; when this was exposed, an edict deposed her.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the princess had a private liaison with a Turk follower of hers; when this was exposed, an edict deposed her.

sentences.zh: 恐都藍不從，遣奇章公牛弘將美妓四人以啖之。

translations.literal: Fearing Dulan would not comply, he sent Niu Hong of Qizhang with four beautiful entertainers to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Dulan would not comply, he sent Niu Hong of Qizhang with four beautiful entertainers to entice him.

sentences.zh: 時沙缽略子曰染幹，號突利可汗，居北方，遣使求婚。

translations.literal: At the time Shaboluo's son Ran Gan, styled Qaghan Tuli, dwelling in the north, sent envoys to request marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shaboluo's son Ran Gan, styled Qaghan Tuli, dwelling in the north, sent envoys to request marriage.

sentences.zh: 上令裴矩謂曰：「當殺大義公主方許婚。」

translations.literal: The emperor had Pei Ju tell him: 'You must kill Princess Dayi before the marriage will be granted.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Pei Ju tell him: 'You must kill Princess Dayi before the marriage will be granted.'

sentences.zh: 突利以為然，復譖之。

translations.literal: Tuli thought this right and slandered her again.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli agreed and slandered her again.

sentences.zh: 都藍因發怒，遂殺公主于帳。

translations.literal: Dulan, in a fit of anger, then killed the princess in the tent.
translations.idiomatic: In his rage Dulan killed the princess in her tent.

sentences.zh: 都藍因與突利可汗有隙，數相征伐，上和解之，各引兵去。

translations.literal: Because Dulan had a rift with Qaghan Tuli, they repeatedly attacked each other; the emperor reconciled them, and each withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dulan and Qaghan Tuli fell out and repeatedly warred on each other; the emperor mediated peace, and both sides withdrew their forces.

sentences.zh: 十七年，突利遣使來逆女，上舍之太常，教習六禮，妻以宗女安義公主。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Tuli sent envoys to fetch his bride; the emperor lodged her with the Chamberlain for Ceremonials and had her taught the Six Rites, and gave him Princess Anyi, a clanswoman.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 Tuli sent envoys to bring home his bride; the emperor housed her in the Court of Imperial Ceremonies to learn the Six Rites, then gave him the imperial clanswoman Princess Anyi in marriage.

sentences.zh: 上欲離間北狄，故特厚其禮，遣牛弘、蘇威、斛律孝卿相繼為使。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to sow discord among the northern Di, and therefore treated him with extraordinary ceremony, sending Niu Hong, Su Wei, and Helü Xiaoqing in succession as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to divide the northern tribes, the emperor lavished extraordinary honors on Tuli and dispatched Niu Hong, Su Wei, and Helü Xiaoqing as envoys one after another.

sentences.zh: 突厥前後遣使入朝，三百七十輩。

translations.literal: The Turks sent envoys to court before and after—370 missions.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks altogether sent 370 missions of envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 突利本居北方，以尚主故，南徙度斤舊鎮，錫賚優厚。

translations.literal: Tuli had originally dwelt in the north; because he had married an imperial princess, he moved south to the old post at Dujin, and was granted gifts with especial generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli had originally lived in the north, but owing to his imperial marriage he moved south to the old Dujin garrison, where he received exceedingly generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭怒曰：「我大可汗也，反不如染幹！」

translations.literal: Yongyulü said in anger: "I am the great qaghan, yet I am treated worse than Ran Gan!'
translations.idiomatic: Yongyulü fumed: "I am the great qaghan, yet I am treated worse than Ran Gan!'

sentences.zh: 於是朝貢遂絕，數為邊患。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute ceased, and he repeatedly menaced the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute ceased, and he became a repeated scourge on the border.

sentences.zh: 十八年，詔蜀王秀出靈州道擊之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, an edict ordered Prince Xiu of Shu to strike them by the Lingzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 an edict ordered Prince Xiu of Shu to attack them along the Lingzhou route.

sentences.zh: 明年，又遣漢王諒為元帥，左僕射高熲率將軍王察、上柱國趙仲卿並出朔州道，右僕射楊素率柱國李徹、韓僧壽出靈州道，上柱國燕榮出幽州，以擊之。

translations.literal: The next year, Prince Liang of Han was again sent as commander-in-chief; Left Vice Director Gao Yong led Generals Wang Cha and Upper Pillar of State Zhao Zhongqing out together by the Shuozhou route; Right Vice Director Yang Su led Pillars of State Li Che and Han Sengshou out by the Lingzhou route; Upper Pillar of State Yan Rong marched from Youzhou—to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Prince Liang of Han was named commander-in-chief; Left Vice Director Gao Yong led General Wang Cha and Upper Pillar of State Zhao Zhongqing along the Shuozhou route; Right Vice Director Yang Su led Pillars of State Li Che and Han Sengshou along the Lingzhou route; Upper Pillar of State Yan Rong marched from Youzhou—all to strike the Turks.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭與玷厥舉兵攻染幹，盡殺其兄弟子女，遂渡河入蔚州。

translations.literal: Yongyulü and Dianjue raised troops to attack Ran Gan, killing all his brothers, sons, and daughters; they then crossed the river and entered Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyulü and Dianjue marched against Ran Gan and slaughtered all his brothers and children; they then crossed the river into Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 染幹夜以五騎與隋使長孫晟歸朝。

translations.literal: By night Ran Gan came to court with five horsemen and the Sui envoy Changsun Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Gan fled by night with five riders and the Sui envoy Changsun Sheng to submit at court.

sentences.zh: 上令染幹與雍虞閭使者因頭特勤相辯詰，染幹辭直，上乃厚待之。

translations.literal: The emperor had Ran Gan and Yongyulü's envoy, Tegin Yintou, debate and cross-examine each other face to face; Ran Gan's words were straightforward, and the emperor therefore treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Ran Gan and Yongyulü's envoy, Tegin Yintou, confront each other in debate; Ran Gan spoke plainly and honestly, and the emperor rewarded him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭弟都速六棄其妻子，與突利歸朝。

translations.literal: Yongyulü's younger brother Dusuliu abandoned his wife and children and came to court with Tuli.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyulü's younger brother Dusuliu abandoned his wife and children and returned to court alongside Tuli.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，敕染幹與都速六樗蒱，稍稍輸以寶物，用歸其心。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this and ordered Ran Gan and Dusuliu to gamble at chapu, gradually letting precious things slip away to him in the game, thereby winning his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and had Ran Gan play chapu with Dusuliu, letting precious goods drift to him little by little in the wagers to win his heart.

sentences.zh: 六月，高熲、楊素擊玷厥，大破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Gao Yong and Yang Su attacked Dianjue and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Gao Yong and Yang Su struck Dianjue and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 拜染幹為意利珍豆啟人可汗，華言意智健也。

translations.literal: Ran Gan was enfeoffed as Qaghan Yili Zhendou Qiren—in Chinese, "wise and healthy."
translations.idiomatic: Ran Gan was invested as Qaghan Yili Zhendou Qiren—Chinese for "wise and stalwart."

sentences.zh: 啟人上表謝恩。

translations.literal: Qiren submitted a memorial thanking him for his grace.
translations.idiomatic: Qiren memorialized the throne in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 上於朔州築大利城以居之。

translations.literal: The emperor built Dali City at Shuozhou to settle him there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built Dali City at Shuozhou for him to inhabit.

sentences.zh: 時安義公主以卒，上以宗女義城公主妻之。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Anyi had died; the emperor gave him the clanswoman Princess Yicheng in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anyi had by then died, and the emperor married him to the clanswoman Princess Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 部落歸者甚眾。

translations.literal: Tribesmen who submitted were exceedingly many.
translations.idiomatic: Vast numbers of tribesmen came over to his side.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭又擊之，上復令入塞。

translations.literal: Yongyulü attacked again; the emperor again had him enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyulü attacked again, and the emperor once more ordered Qiren within the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭侵掠不已，遂遷于河南，在夏、勝二州間，發徒掘塹數百里，東西距河，盡為啟人畜牧地。

translations.literal: Yongyulü's raids never ceased; Qiren was therefore relocated to the region south of the Yellow River, between Xia and Sheng prefectures; corvée laborers were sent to dig trenches for several hundred li, stretching east and west from the river—all becoming pasture for Qiren.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yongyulü's raids never stopped, Qiren was moved south of the Yellow River, between Xia and Sheng prefectures; laborers dug trenches for hundreds of li from the river east to west, all reserved as pasture for Qiren's people.

sentences.zh: 於是遣越國公楊素出靈州，行軍總管韓僧壽出慶州，太平公史萬歲出燕州，大將軍姚辯出河州，以擊都藍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Duke Yang Su of Yue was sent out from Lingzhou; Military Governor Han Sengshou from Qingzhou; Duke Shi Wansui of Taiping from Yanzhou; and General Yao Bian from Hezhou—to attack Dulan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dispatched Duke Yang Su of Yue from Lingzhou, Military Governor Han Sengshou from Qingzhou, Duke Shi Wansui of Taiping from Yanzhou, and General Yao Bian from Hezhou to attack Dulan.

sentences.zh: 師未出塞，而都藍為其麾下所殺，達頭自立為步伽可汗，其國大亂。

translations.literal: Before the armies had left the frontier, Dulan was killed by his own subordinates; Datou installed himself as Qaghan Buga, and the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies could cross the frontier, Dulan was killed by his own followers; Datou proclaimed himself Qaghan Buga, and the realm descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 遣太平公史萬歲出朔州以擊之，遇達頭於大斤山，虜不戰而遁。

translations.literal: Duke Shi Wansui of Taiping was sent out from Shuozhou to attack him; he met Datou at Mt. Dajin, and the barbarians fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Shi Wansui of Taiping was sent from Shuozhou to pursue him; at Mt. Dajin he encountered Datou, and the Turks fled without giving battle.

sentences.zh: 尋遣其子侯利伐徒磧東攻啟人，上又發兵助啟人守要路，侯利伐退走入磧。

translations.literal: Before long he sent his son Helifa east across the desert sands to attack Qiren; the emperor again dispatched troops to help Qiren hold the strategic passes, and Helifa withdrew into the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Buga sent his son Helifa east across the sands to attack Qiren; the emperor again sent troops to help Qiren hold the key passes, and Helifa retreated back into the desert.

sentences.zh: 啟人上表陳謝曰：「大隋聖人莫緣可汗憐養，百姓蒙恩，赤心歸服，或南入長城，或住白道。

translations.literal: Qiren submitted a memorial of thanks, saying: "The sage Mo-yuan Qaghan of great Sui nurtured us; the people received his grace; with devoted hearts we submitted—some entering south of the Great Wall, some dwelling along the White Road.
translations.idiomatic: Qiren memorialized in gratitude: "The sage Mo-yuan Qaghan of great Sui has sheltered us; our people have received his grace; with loyal hearts we have submitted—some living south of the Great Wall, some dwelling along the White Road.

sentences.zh: 染幹如枯木重起枝葉，枯骨重生皮肉，千世萬世，長與大隋典羊、馬也。」

translations.literal: Ran Gan is like a withered tree sprouting branches and leaves anew, or dead bones regrowing flesh and skin; for a thousand and ten thousand generations he will forever herd sheep and horses for great Sui."
translations.idiomatic: Ran Gan is like a withered tree putting forth leaves again, like dead bones growing flesh anew; for ten thousand generations he will forever tend sheep and horses for great Sui."

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，代州總管韓洪為虜敗于恆安，詔楊素為雲州道行軍元帥，率啟人北征。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, Regional Inspector Han Hong of Daizhou was defeated by the barbarians at Heng'an; Yang Su was ordered as commander-in-chief on the Yunzhou route and led Qiren on a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou, Regional Inspector Han Hong of Daizhou was defeated by the Turks at Heng'an; Yang Su was appointed commander-in-chief on the Yunzhou route and led Qiren north in expedition.

sentences.zh: 斛薛等諸姓初附於啟人，至是而叛。

translations.literal: The various clans such as Huxie had at first submitted to Qiren; at this time they rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Clans such as the Huxie had first submitted to Qiren, but now they rebelled.

sentences.zh: 素軍河北，逢突厥阿勿思力俟斤等南渡，掠啟人男女雜畜而去，素率上大將軍梁默追之，大破俟斤，悉得人畜以歸啟人。

translations.literal: Yang Su's army was north of the river when he encountered the Turks Aosili Yijin and others crossing south, plundering Qiren's men and women and mixed herds and driving them off; Yang Su led Senior General Liang Mo in pursuit, routed Yijin completely, and returned all the people and livestock to Qiren.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Su's army was north of the river, the Turks Aosili Yijin and others crossed south and raided Qiren's people and herds; Yang Su led Senior General Liang Mo in pursuit, routed Yijin, and restored all the captives and livestock to Qiren.

sentences.zh: 素又遣柱國張定和、領軍大將軍劉升別路邀擊，並多斬獲而還。

translations.literal: Yang Su also sent Pillars of State Zhang Dinghe and Lieutenant General Liu Sheng by separate routes to intercept and attack; both returned with many heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su also sent Pillars of State Zhang Dinghe and Lieutenant General Liu Sheng by separate routes to ambush the enemy; both returned with heavy slaughter and many captives.

sentences.zh: 兵既渡河，賊復掠啟人部落，素率驃騎范貴于窟結谷東南復破之。

translations.literal: Once the army had crossed the river, the bandits again plundered Qiren's tribes; Yang Su led Rapid-Cavalry General Fan Gui and again routed them southeast of Kujie Valley.
translations.idiomatic: After the army had crossed the river, the raiders struck Qiren's tribes again; Yang Su led Rapid-Cavalry General Fan Gui and defeated them once more southeast of Kujie Valley.

sentences.zh: 是歲，泥利可汗及葉護俱被鐵勒所敗，步迦尋亦大亂。

translations.literal: That year both Qaghan Nili and Yehu were defeated by the Tiele; before long Buga also fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: That year both Nili Qaghan and Yehu were defeated by the Tiele, and before long Buga too was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 奚、雪五部內徙，步伽奔吐谷渾，啟人遂有其眾，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: The five tribes Xi and Xue moved inward; Buga fled to the Tuyuhun; Qiren then took over their followers and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The five Xi and Xue tribes migrated inward; Buga fled to the Tuyuhun; Qiren then absorbed their people and sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，煬帝幸榆林，啟人及義城公主來朝行宮，前後獻馬三千匹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, Emperor Yang visited Yulin; Qiren and Princess Yicheng came to audience at the traveling palace and presented three thousand horses before and after.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 3 Emperor Yang visited Yulin; Qiren and Princess Yicheng came to the touring palace and presented three thousand horses in all.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜帛萬三千段。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted thirteen thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and granted thirteen thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 啟人及義城公主上表曰：「已前聖人先帝莫緣可汗存日，憐臣，賜臣安義公主，臣種末為聖人先帝憐養。

translations.literal: Qiren and Princess Yicheng submitted a memorial, saying: "In former days, while the sage prior emperor Mo-yuan Qaghan lived, he pitied your servant and granted your servant Princess Anyi; the last of my people were nurtured by the sage prior emperor's pity.
translations.idiomatic: Qiren and Princess Yicheng memorialized: "In days past, while the sage prior emperor Mo-yuan Qaghan still lived, he took pity on me and gave me Princess Anyi; the remnant of my people were kept alive by the sage prior emperor's compassion.

sentences.zh: 臣兄弟妒惡，相共殺臣。

translations.literal: My brothers, jealous and vicious, joined together to kill me.
translations.idiomatic: My brothers, consumed by envy, plotted together to kill me.

sentences.zh: 臣當時無處去，向上看只見天，下看只見地，實憶聖人先帝言語，投命去來。

translations.literal: At the time your servant had nowhere to go—looking up I saw only heaven, looking down only earth; I truly remembered the sage prior emperor's words and came to cast my life upon him.
translations.idiomatic: I had nowhere to turn—above me only sky, below me only earth; I remembered the sage prior emperor's words and came to give my life into his hands.

sentences.zh: 聖人先帝見臣，大憐臣死命，養活勝於往前，遣臣作大可汗坐著也。

translations.literal: When the sage prior emperor saw your servant, he greatly pitied my perishing life and kept me alive better than before, and sent me to sit as great qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage prior emperor received me, he spared my life and kept me alive better than ever, and installed me to sit as great qaghan.

sentences.zh: 突厥百姓死者以外，還聚集作百姓也。

translations.literal: Apart from those of the Turkic people who died, the rest have gathered and become a people again.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from those who died, the Turkic people have gathered again and live as a people once more.

sentences.zh: 至尊今還如聖人先帝于天下四方坐也，還養活臣及突厥百姓，實無少短。

translations.literal: Your Majesty now sits as the sage prior emperor did over all the world in the four directions, and still nurtures your servant and the Turkic people—truly without the least failing.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now sits over the four quarters as the sage prior emperor did, still sustaining me and the Turkic people—not the least bit lacking.

sentences.zh: 至尊憐臣時，乞依大國，服飾法用一同華夏。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty shows pity on your servant, I beg to follow the great state and make dress and customs identical with Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty shows me kindness, I beg to follow the great state and adopt dress and customs the same as China.

sentences.zh: 帝下其議，公卿請依所奏，帝以為不可。

translations.literal: The emperor referred the memorial for deliberation; the high officials asked that it be granted as requested, but the emperor deemed it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the petition for discussion; the chief ministers urged approval, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：「君子教人，不求變俗，何必化諸削衽，縻以長纓？」

translations.literal: An edict then said: "The gentleman teaches others but does not seek to change their customs—why must we transform them by cutting their robes and binding them with long tassels?"
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "The gentleman teaches others but does not seek to alter their customs—why must we make them cut their robes and bind them with court sashes?"

sentences.zh: 乃璽書答啟人，以為磧北未靜，猶復征戰，但使存心孝順，何必改衣服也。

translations.literal: An imperial letter under seal was sent in reply to Qiren, saying that north of the desert was not yet at peace and warfare continued; so long as his heart remained devoted and obedient, why need he change his dress?
translations.idiomatic: An edict under the imperial seal answered Qiren: the north beyond the sands was still unsettled and fighting continued, but so long as he kept a loyal heart, what need was there to change his clothing?

sentences.zh: 帝法駕御千人大帳，享啟人及其部落酋長三千五百人，賜物二千段，其下各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor in his full imperial carriage presided in a great tent for a thousand men and feasted Qiren and thirty-five hundred chieftains of his tribes, granting two thousand bolts of goods; those below each received according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in full imperial panoply, presided in a great tent seating a thousand and feasted Qiren and thirty-five hundred tribal chiefs, granting two thousand bolts of goods in all, with gradations below.

sentences.zh: 復下詔褒寵之，賜路車、乘馬、鼓吹、幡旗，贊拜不名，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: Another edict commended and honored him, granting a state carriage, riding horses, musical escort, banners and flags, applause at audience without calling his name, and rank above the feudal princes and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict praised and honored him, granting a ceremonial carriage, riding horses, a musical escort, banners and flags, obeisance without calling his name, and a rank above all feudal princes.

sentences.zh: 帝親巡雲中，溯金河而東，北幸啟人所居。

translations.literal: The emperor personally toured Yunzhong, followed the Jin River eastward, and proceeded north to the place where Qiren dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally toured Yunzhong, traced the Jin River eastward, and traveled north to visit where Qiren lived.

sentences.zh: 啟人奉觴上壽，跪伏甚恭。

translations.literal: Qiren raised a cup and offered longevity; kneeling prostrate, he was exceedingly deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Qiren raised a cup and offered blessings on the emperor's life, kneeling prostrate in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賦詩曰：「鹿塞鴻旗駐，龍庭翠輦回，氈帳望風舉，穹廬向日開。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and composed a poem, saying: "At Lusai the wild-goose banners halt; from the dragon court the green carriage returns; felt tents rise at our passing breeze; domed lodges open toward the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and composed a poem: "At Lusai the wild-goose banners stand; from the dragon court the green carriage returns; felt tents rise at our passing wind; domed lodges open toward the sun.

sentences.zh: 呼韓頓顙至，屠耆接踵來，索辮擎膻肉，韋韌獻酒杯。

translations.literal: Khans bow their heads as Huhanye did; chieftains come one after another; braided queues hold up mutton; leather flasks present wine cups.
translations.idiomatic: Khans bow their heads as Huhanye once did; chieftains flock in succession; braided hair offers mutton; leather flasks hold out wine cups.

sentences.zh: 何如漢天子，空上單于台？」

translations.literal: How does this compare with the Han Son of Heaven, who vainly climbed the Shanyu Terrace alone?'
translations.idiomatic: How unlike the Son of Han, who climbed the Shanyu Terrace to no purpose?'

sentences.zh: 帝賜啟人及主金甕各一，及衣服、被褥、錦彩；

translations.literal: The emperor granted Qiren and the princess each a gold jar, as well as clothing, bedding, and brocades;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Qiren and the princess each a golden jar, along with clothing, bedding, and brocades;

sentences.zh: 特勤以下各有差。

translations.literal: Those below the tegin each received according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Those of tegin rank and below received gifts according to their station.

sentences.zh: 先是，高麗私通使啟人所，啟人不敢隱境外之交，是日，持高麗使見。

translations.literal: Earlier, Goryeo had secretly sent envoys to Qiren's domain; Qiren did not dare hide intercourse beyond the frontier, and that day led the Goryeo envoy forward for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Goryeo had secretly dispatched envoys to Qiren's camp; Qiren did not dare conceal dealings beyond the border, and that day brought the Goryeo envoy before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 敕令牛弘宣旨謂曰：「朕以啟人誠長奉國，故親至其所。

translations.literal: An order commanded Niu Hong to proclaim the imperial intent, saying: "Because Qiren has long served the state in good faith, I have come in person to his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Niu Hong to declare his intent: "Because Qiren has long remained loyal to the state, I have come in person to his camp.

sentences.zh: 明年當往涿郡。

translations.literal: Next year I shall go to Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Next year I shall travel to Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 爾回日，語高麗主，宜早來朝。」

translations.literal: On your return, tell the king of Goryeo that he should come early to court.'
translations.idiomatic: When you return, tell the king of Goryeo to come to court without delay.'

sentences.zh: 使人甚懼。

translations.literal: The envoy was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was terrified.

sentences.zh: 啟人乃扈從入塞至定襄，詔令歸蕃。

translations.literal: Qiren then escorted the emperor within the passes to Dingxiang; an edict ordered him to return to his tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Qiren then escorted the court within the passes as far as Dingxiang, where an edict sent him back to his domains.

sentences.zh: 明年，朝於東都，禮賜益厚。

translations.literal: The next year he attended court at the eastern capital; ceremonial gifts grew ever richer.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he attended court at the eastern capital, and ceremonial gifts grew richer still.

sentences.zh: 是歲，疾終，上為廢朝三日。

translations.literal: That year he died of illness; the emperor suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died of illness, and the emperor suspended court for three days in mourning.

sentences.zh: 其子吐吉立，是為始畢可汗。

translations.literal: His son Tuji was installed—this was Qaghan Shibi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuji succeeded him as Qaghan Shibi.

sentences.zh: 表續尚公主，詔從其俗。

translations.literal: Tuji requested to continue marrying an imperial princess; an edict followed their custom.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi asked to continue the imperial marriage alliance; an edict permitted it according to Turkic custom.

sentences.zh: 十一年，來朝於東都。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he came to court at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he attended court at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 其年，車駕避暑汾陽宮。

translations.literal: That same year the imperial carriage summered at Fenyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the emperor summered at Fenyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 八月，始畢率其種落入寇，圍帝於雁門。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Shibi led his tribesmen in raids and surrounded the emperor at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shibi led his people in invasion and besieged the emperor at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 援兵方至，始畢引去。

translations.literal: Relief troops were just arriving when Shibi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces were just arriving when Shibi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 由是朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: From this tribute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From that point tribute ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 明年，復寇馬邑，唐公擊走之。

translations.literal: The next year he raided again at Mayi; the Duke of Tang drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he raided Mayi again; the Duke of Tang routed him.

sentences.zh: 隋末亂離，中國人歸之者無數，遂大強盛。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, amid turmoil and dispersal, countless Chinese submitted to him, and he became greatly powerful.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos at the end of Sui, countless Chinese defected to him, and his power grew vastly.

sentences.zh: 迎蕭后置於定襄。

translations.literal: He welcomed Empress Xiao and established her at Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed Empress Xiao and installed her at Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 薛舉、竇建德、王世充、劉武周、梁師都、李軌、高開道之徒，雖僭尊號，皆稱臣，受其可汗之號，使者往來，相望於道。

translations.literal: Xue Ju, Dou Jiande, Wang Shichong, Liu Wuzhou, Liang Shidu, Li Gui, Gao Kaidao, and the like—though they usurped royal titles—all called themselves his vassals, accepted qaghan titles from him, and their envoys passed one another unceasingly on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju, Dou Jiande, Wang Shichong, Liu Wuzhou, Liang Shidu, Li Gui, Gao Kaidao, and the like all styled themselves his vassals though they had usurped thrones, accepted qaghan titles from him, and their envoys crowded the roads in endless passage.

sentences.zh: 西突厥

translations.literal: Western Turks
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turks

sentences.zh: 西突厥者，木杆可汗之子大邏便也。

translations.literal: As for the Western Turks, they were Daluobian, son of Qaghan Mugan.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turks were descended from Daluobian, son of Qaghan Mugan.

sentences.zh: 與沙缽略有隙，因分為二，漸以強盛。

translations.literal: He had a rift with Shaboluo and therefore split into two; they gradually grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Estranged from Shaboluo, they split in two and gradually grew powerful.

sentences.zh: 東拒都斤，西至龜茲，鐵勒、伊吾及西域諸胡悉附之。

translations.literal: East they held at Dujin, west to Kucha; the Tiele, Yiwu, and all the Hu peoples of the Western Regions submitted to them.
translations.idiomatic: Their domain ran from Dujin in the east to Kucha in the west; the Tiele, Yiwu, and all the peoples of the Western Regions submitted to them.

sentences.zh: 大邏便為處邏侯所執，其國立鞅素特勤之子，是為泥利可汗。

translations.literal: Daluobian was seized by Chuluohou; the state installed the son of Tegin Yangsu—this was Qaghan Nili.
translations.idiomatic: Daluobian was seized by Chuluohou, and the realm installed the son of Tegin Yangsu as Qaghan Nili.

sentences.zh: 卒，子達漫立，號泥撅處羅可汗。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Daman was installed, styled Qaghan Nijue Chuluo.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son Daman succeeded, styled Qaghan Nijue Chuluo.

sentences.zh: 其母向氏，本中國人，生達漫而泥利卒，向氏又嫁其弟婆實特勤。

translations.literal: His mother was the Xiang clan—a Chinese originally; she bore Daman and Nili died; Lady Xiang then married his younger brother Tegin Boshi.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Xiang, was originally Chinese; she bore Daman, and after Nili's death she married his younger brother Tegin Boshi.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，婆實共向氏入朝，遇達頭之亂，遂留京師，每舍之鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, Boshi came to court with Lady Xiang; they encountered Datou's revolt and therefore remained in the capital, lodging each time at the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaihuang, Boshi and Lady Xiang came to court; Datou's revolt broke out and they remained in the capital, lodged each visit at the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 處羅可汗居無恆處，終多在烏孫故地。

translations.literal: Qaghan Chuluo had no fixed dwelling and mostly stayed in the former lands of the Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Chuluo had no fixed seat and mostly ranged through the old Wusun territory.

sentences.zh: 復立二小可汗，分統所部，一在石國北，以制諸胡國；

translations.literal: He again set up two lesser qaghans to divide rule over the tribes—one north of Shiguo to control the Hu states;
translations.idiomatic: He also installed two lesser qaghans to govern his divisions—one north of Shiguo to control the Hu states;

sentences.zh: 一居龜茲北，其地名應娑。

translations.literal: one dwelt north of Kucha, at a place called Yingsuo.
translations.idiomatic: one lived north of Kucha at a place called Yingsuo.

sentences.zh: 官有俟發、閻洪達，以評議國事，自余與東國同。

translations.literal: In office were Yifa and Yan Hongda to deliberate state affairs; the rest was the same as the Eastern Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Officials included Yifa and Yan Hongda to deliberate on state affairs; the rest matched the eastern realm.

sentences.zh: 每五月、八月，聚祭神，歲使重臣向其先世所居之窟致祭焉。

translations.literal: Every fifth and eighth month they gathered to sacrifice to the gods; each year a high minister was sent to the cave where their forebears had dwelt to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Every fifth and eighth month they gathered for sacrifices to the gods; each year a senior minister was sent to the cave where their ancestors had lived to offer worship.

sentences.zh: 當大業初，處羅可汗撫禦無道，其國多叛，與鐵勒屢相攻，大為鐵勒所敗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, Qaghan Chuluo governed without the Way; many in his realm rebelled, and he repeatedly fought the Tiele, suffering great defeats at their hands.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daye reign Qaghan Chuluo ruled without justice; his realm rebelled widely, and repeated wars with the Tiele brought him heavy defeat.

sentences.zh: 時黃門侍郎裴矩在敦煌引致西域，聞其國亂，復知處羅思其母氏，因奏之。

translations.literal: At the time Yellow Gate Vice Director Pei Ju was in Dunhuang receiving submissions from the Western Regions; hearing of the realm's disorder and learning that Chuluo missed his mother, he memorialized about this.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Pei Ju was then in Dunhuang cultivating ties with the Western Regions; learning of the realm's chaos and that Chuluo longed for his mother, he memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣司朝謁者崔君肅齎書慰諭之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang dispatched Protocol Officer Cui Junsu bearing a letter to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Protocol Officer Cui Junsu with an imperial letter of consolation.

sentences.zh: 處羅甚踞，受詔不肯起。

translations.literal: Chuluo was very haughty; receiving the edict he refused to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo was exceedingly arrogant; when the edict was read he would not rise.

sentences.zh: 君肅謂處羅曰：「突厥本一國也，中分為二，自相仇敵，每歲交兵，積十年而莫能相滅者，明知啟人與處羅國其勢敵耳。

translations.literal: Junsu said to Chuluo: "The Turks were originally one realm, split in two and mutually hostile; year after year they fought, and for ten years neither could destroy the other—this clearly shows that Qiren's state and Chuluo's state are evenly matched.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu said to Chuluo: "The Turks were once one realm, then divided in two and turned on each other; for ten years they fought without either side prevailing—that alone shows Qiren's power matches yours.

sentences.zh: 今啟人舉其部落，兵且百萬，入臣天子，甚有丹誠者，何也？

translations.literal: Now Qiren has led his tribes—nearly a million troops—and entered submission to the Son of Heaven with utmost sincerity. Why?
translations.idiomatic: Now Qiren has brought his tribes—nearly a million strong—and submitted to the Son of Heaven with open-hearted loyalty. Why is that?

sentences.zh: 但以切恨可汗而不能獨制，故卑事天子以借漢兵，連二大國，欲滅可汗耳。

translations.literal: Only because he bitterly hates Your Qaghanship yet cannot overcome him alone, he humbles himself before the Son of Heaven to borrow Han troops, joining two great realms in order to destroy Your Qaghanship.
translations.idiomatic: Because he hates you deeply but cannot overcome you alone, he humbles himself before the Son of Heaven to borrow Chinese troops—uniting two great powers to destroy you.

sentences.zh: 百官兆庶咸請許之，天子弗違，師出有日矣。

translations.literal: All the hundred offices and the myriad people ask that this be granted; the Son of Heaven will not refuse—a campaign is only days away.
translations.idiomatic: Every official and subject has urged approval; the Son of Heaven will not refuse—a campaign will launch any day now.

sentences.zh: 顧可汗母向氏，本中國人，歸在京師，處於賓館，聞天子之詔，懼可汗之滅，旦夕守闕，哭甚悲哀，是以天子憐焉，為其輟策。

translations.literal: But Your Qaghan's mother, Lady Xiang, is originally Chinese and lives in the capital at the guest lodge; hearing the Son of Heaven's decree, she feared Your Qaghan's destruction and day and night kept vigil at the palace gates, weeping most piteously—thus the Son of Heaven took pity and for her sake halted the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: But your mother Lady Xiang, a Chinese woman living in the capital guesthouse, heard the emperor's decree and feared for your destruction; day and night she kept vigil at the palace gates, weeping bitterly—so the Son of Heaven took pity and for her sake stayed the campaign.

sentences.zh: 向夫人又匍匐謝罪，因請發使以召可汗，令入內屬，乞加恩禮，同於啟人。

translations.literal: Lady Xiang again crawled prostrate to beg forgiveness and asked that envoys be sent to summon Your Qaghan, to enter inner allegiance, and seek favor and ceremony equal to Qiren's.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiang then crawled forward to beg forgiveness and asked that envoys be sent to summon you to submit within the passes, seeking honors equal to Qiren's.

sentences.zh: 天子從之，遣使到此。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven consented and sent envoys here.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven agreed and sent envoys here.

sentences.zh: 可汗若稱籓拜詔，國乃永安，而母得延壽；

translations.literal: If Your Qaghan declares himself a vassal and does obeisance to receive the edict, the state will then be forever secure, and Your Mother will attain extended years;
translations.idiomatic: If you declare yourself a vassal and bow to receive the edict, your realm will be secure and your mother will live out her years;

sentences.zh: 不然者，則向夫人為誑天子，必當取戮而傳首虜庭。

translations.literal: Otherwise, Lady Xiang has deceived the Son of Heaven and will surely be executed, her head sent to the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Lady Xiang will be judged to have deceived the emperor—she will be executed and her head sent to your court.

sentences.zh: 發大隋之兵，資北蕃之眾，左提右挈，以擊可汗，死亡則無日矣！

translations.literal: Mobilizing Great Sui's troops, supplying the northern frontier peoples' masses, leading with the left hand and supporting with the right to strike Your Qaghan—death will be only days away!
translations.idiomatic: Great Sui will mobilize its armies, supply the northern tribes, and strike from every side—your death will be only days away!

sentences.zh: 奈何惜兩拜之禮，剿慈母之命，吝一句稱臣，喪匈奴之國也？」

translations.literal: How can you begrudge two bows of ceremony, destroy your loving mother's life, be stingy with one phrase of declaring yourself subject, and lose the Xiongnu state?'
translations.idiomatic: Why cling to two bows of ceremony, throw away your mother's life, refuse one phrase of submission, and lose your realm?

sentences.zh: 處羅聞之，瞿然而起，流涕再拜，跪受詔書。

translations.literal: Chuluo heard this, started up with a start, wept and bowed twice, and knelt to receive the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo heard this, started up in alarm, wept and bowed twice, then knelt to receive the edict.

sentences.zh: 君肅又說處羅曰：「啟人內附，先帝嘉之，賞賜極厚，故致兵強國富。

translations.literal: Junsu again persuaded Chuluo, saying: "When Qiren submitted within the passes, the prior emperor praised him and rewarded him exceedingly richly, thus making his troops strong and his state wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu again urged Chuluo: "When Qiren submitted within the passes, the late emperor praised him and gave lavish rewards, making his army strong and his realm rich.

sentences.zh: 今可汗後附，與之爭寵，須深結于天子，自表至誠。

translations.literal: Now Your Qaghan has submitted later; to compete with him for favor you must forge deep ties with the Son of Heaven and show utter sincerity yourself.
translations.idiomatic: You have submitted later and must compete with him for favor—you need deep ties with the Son of Heaven and a show of utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 既以遠道，未得朝覲，宜立一功，以明臣節。」

translations.literal: Since you are on a distant road and have not been able to attend court, you should establish a merit to demonstrate the loyalty of a subject."
translations.idiomatic: You are far away and cannot yet attend court—you should perform some service to prove your loyalty."

sentences.zh: 處羅曰：「如何？」

translations.literal: Chuluo said: "How?"
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo asked: "How?"

sentences.zh: 君肅曰：「吐谷渾者，啟人少子莫賀咄設之母家也。

translations.literal: Junsu said: "The Tuyuhun are the maternal clan of Qiren's youngest son, Mouhezhusi she.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu said: "The Tuyuhun are the maternal kin of Qiren's youngest son, Mouhezhusi she.

sentences.zh: 今天子又以義城公主妻于啟人，畏天子之威，而與之絕。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven has also given Princess Yicheng in marriage to Qiren; fearing the Son of Heaven's might, he will break with them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has now given Princess Yicheng to Qiren in marriage; fearing imperial might, Qiren will break with the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾亦因憾漢，職貢不修。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun likewise, bearing resentment toward Han, have neglected tribute and offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun too, resentful toward China, have neglected tribute.

sentences.zh: 可汗若請誅之，天子必許。

translations.literal: If Your Qaghan requests permission to punish them, the Son of Heaven will surely grant it.
translations.idiomatic: If you ask permission to punish them, the emperor will surely agree.

sentences.zh: 漢擊其內，可汗攻其外，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Han strikes from within, Your Qaghan attacks from without—they will surely be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: China will strike from within and you from without—they cannot fail to be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 然後自入朝，道路無阻，因見老母，不亦可乎？」

translations.literal: Then you may yourself enter court—the road will be unobstructed, and you may see your old mother—is this not well?"
translations.idiomatic: Then you can come to court yourself—the road will be clear, and you can see your mother. Would that not be best?

sentences.zh: 處羅大喜，遂遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Chuluo was greatly delighted and forthwith sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo was delighted and at once sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝將四狩，六年，遣侍御史韋節召處羅，令與車駕會於大鬥拔穀。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to conduct his fourth hunt; in the sixth year he sent Supervising Censor Wei Jie to summon Chuluo, ordering him to meet the imperial carriage at Dadoubaga.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned his fourth hunt, in the sixth year he sent Supervising Censor Wei Jie to summon Chuluo and meet the imperial procession at Dadoubaga.

sentences.zh: 其國人不從，處羅謝使者，辭以他故。

translations.literal: His countrymen would not follow; Chuluo apologized to the envoy, declining on other pretexts.
translations.idiomatic: His people refused to go; Chuluo apologized to the envoy and pleaded other reasons.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，無如之何。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered but could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious but could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 適會其酋長射匱遣使來求婚，裴矩奏曰：「處羅不朝，恃強大耳。

translations.literal: Just then their chieftain Shegui sent envoys to request marriage; Pei Ju memorialized: "Chuluo does not attend court only because he relies on his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Just then their chieftain Shegui sent envoys to request marriage. Pei Ju memorialized: "Chuluo stays away only because he trusts in his power.

sentences.zh: 臣請以計弱之，分裂其國，即易制也。

translations.literal: Your subject asks to use stratagem to weaken him; split his state and he will then be easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to weaken him by stratagem—split his realm and he will be easy to manage.

sentences.zh: 射匱者，都六之子，達頭之孫，世為可汗，君臨西面。

translations.literal: Shegui is the son of Duliu and grandson of Tatou, for generations a qaghan ruling the western domain.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui is Duliu's son and Tatou's grandson—a hereditary qaghan ruling the west.

sentences.zh: 今聞其失職，附隸于處羅，故遣使來以結援。

translations.literal: Now hearing he had lost his position and submitted to Chuluo, he sent envoys to forge an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost his standing and submitted to Chuluo, he now sends envoys seeking support.

sentences.zh: 願厚禮其使，拜為大可汗，則突厥勢分，兩從我矣。」

translations.literal: I wish to treat his envoys with rich ceremony and invest him as Great Qaghan; then the Turks' power will be divided and both will follow us."
translations.idiomatic: Let us honor his envoys richly and invest him as Great Qaghan—the Turks will be divided and both will follow us."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 因遣裴矩，朝夕至館，微諷喻之。

translations.literal: He then sent Pei Ju, who morning and evening visited the lodge, subtly persuading them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Pei Ju to visit the envoys' lodge morning and evening, gently urging them.

sentences.zh: 帝於仁風殿召其使者，言處羅不順之意，稱射匱有好心，吾將立為大可汗，令發兵誅處羅，然後當為婚也。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned their envoys at Renfeng Hall, spoke of Chuluo's disobedience, praised Shegui's good intentions, and said he would establish him as Great Qaghan, ordering him to raise troops to punish Chuluo—then the marriage would be granted.
translations.idiomatic: At Renfeng Hall the emperor summoned the envoys, spoke of Chuluo's defiance, praised Shegui's goodwill, and said he would make Shegui Great Qaghan if he raised troops to punish Chuluo—then the marriage would follow.

sentences.zh: 取桃竹白羽箭一枚以賜射匱，因謂之曰：「此事宜速，使疾如箭也。」

translations.literal: He took one peach-bamboo white-feather arrow and bestowed it upon Shegui, and told them: "This matter should be hurried—be swift as an arrow."
translations.idiomatic: He gave Shegui one white-feather arrow of peach bamboo and said: "Act quickly—be swift as this arrow.

sentences.zh: 使者返，路經處羅。

translations.literal: The envoys returned by a route passing through Chuluo's territory.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys returned by way of Chuluo's territory.

sentences.zh: 愛其箭，將留之，使者譎而得免。

translations.literal: He admired the arrow and meant to keep it; the envoys by cunning got free.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo admired the arrow and tried to keep it; the envoys tricked their way free.

sentences.zh: 射匱聞而大喜，興兵襲之，處羅大敗，棄妻子，將左右數千騎東走。

translations.literal: Shegui heard and was greatly delighted; he raised troops and attacked; Chuluo was utterly defeated, abandoned his wife and children, and fled east with several thousand horsemen of his retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui heard and rejoiced; he raised troops and attacked. Chuluo was routed, abandoned his wife and children, and fled east with a few thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 在路又被劫掠，遁于高昌，車保時羅漫山。

translations.literal: On the road he was robbed again; he fled to Gaochang and took refuge on Mount Luomanshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he was robbed again; he fled to Gaochang and took refuge on Mount Luomanshan.

sentences.zh: 高昌王麹伯雅上狀，帝遣裴矩將向氏親要左右，馳至玉門關晉昌城。

translations.literal: The King of Gaochang, Qu Boya, submitted a report; the emperor sent Pei Ju with Lady Xiang's relatives and attendants, galloping to Jinchang city at Yumen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: King Qu Boya of Gaochang reported this; the emperor sent Pei Ju with Lady Xiang's kin and attendants, galloping to Jinchang at Yumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 矩遣向氏使詣處羅所，論朝廷弘養之義，丁甯曉喻之。

translations.literal: Ju sent Lady Xiang's party to Chuluo's place to expound the court's broad nurture and care, earnestly instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju sent Lady Xiang's party to Chuluo to explain the court's generous care and earnestly persuade him.

sentences.zh: 遂入朝，然每有怏怏之色。

translations.literal: He then entered court, yet always wore a discontented expression.
translations.idiomatic: He then came to court, but always looked discontented.

sentences.zh: 以七年冬，處羅朝于臨朔宮。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year Chuluo attended court at Linshuo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year Chuluo attended court at Linshuo Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝享之，處羅稽首謝曰：「臣總西面諸蕃，不得早來朝拜，今參見遲晚，罪責極深。

translations.literal: The emperor feasted him; Chuluo kowtowed and apologized: "Your subject oversees the various barbarians of the west and could not come earlier to attend court; now my audience is late—my guilt and blame run extremely deep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted him. Chuluo kowtowed and apologized: "I govern the western tribes and could not come sooner; this late audience brings deep guilt.

sentences.zh: 臣心裏悚懼，不能盡道。」

translations.literal: In my heart I am fearful and trembling and cannot fully express it."
translations.idiomatic: My heart is full of fear and I cannot say all I feel."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「往者與突厥遞相侵擾，不得安居。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Formerly Turks and we harassed one another in turn and could not live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In the past Turks and we raided each other in turn and neither side could live in peace.

sentences.zh: 今四海既清，與一家無異，朕皆欲存養，使遂性靈。

translations.literal: Now the four seas are clear and we are no different from one family; I wish to preserve and nurture all and let them follow their natures.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace and we are one family; I wish to preserve and nurture all peoples and let them live as they will.

sentences.zh: 譬如上天，止有一個日照臨，莫不寧帖；

translations.literal: It is like Heaven above—there is only one sun shining upon all, and none are not at peace;
translations.idiomatic: It is like Heaven—there is only one sun shining on all, and everyone is at peace;

sentences.zh: 若有兩個、三個日，萬物何以得安？

translations.literal: if there were two or three suns, how could the myriad things find peace?
translations.idiomatic: if there were two or three suns, how could anything live in peace?

sentences.zh: 比者，亦知處羅總攝事繁，不得早來相見。

translations.literal: Of late I also knew that Chuluo, overseeing many affairs, could not come earlier to meet.
translations.idiomatic: I also knew you were burdened with many affairs and could not come sooner.

sentences.zh: 今日見處羅，懷抱豁然歡喜。

translations.literal: Today, seeing Chuluo, my breast is suddenly opened with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Today, seeing you, my heart is suddenly glad.

sentences.zh: 處羅亦當豁然，不煩在意。」

translations.literal: Chuluo too should be suddenly at ease and need not trouble his mind."
translations.idiomatic: You too should be at ease and put your worries aside."

sentences.zh: 明年元會，處羅上壽曰：「自天以下，地以上，日月所照，唯有聖人可汗。

translations.literal: The next year at the New Year assembly Chuluo offered longevity-wishes: "From Heaven below to Earth above, where sun and moon shine, there is none but the Sage Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The next New Year Chuluo offered a toast: "From Heaven to Earth, wherever sun and moon shine, only the Sage Qaghan exists.

sentences.zh: 今是大日，願聖人可汗千歲、萬歲，常如今日也。」

translations.literal: Now is the Great Sun; may the Sage Qaghan live a thousand years, ten thousand years, ever as today."
translations.idiomatic: Today is the Great Sun; may the Sage Qaghan live a thousand, ten thousand years, always as today.

sentences.zh: 詔留其羸弱萬餘口，令其弟達度闕設牧畜會寧郡。

translations.literal: By edict the weak and infirm—more than ten thousand mouths—were left behind, and his younger brother Dadu Que she was ordered to herd livestock in Huining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict left more than ten thousand of the weak behind and ordered his younger brother Dadu Que she to pasture livestock in Huining Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 處羅從征高麗，號為曷薩那可汗，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Chuluo accompanied the campaign against Goryeo and was titled Hesana Qaghan; rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo joined the campaign against Goryeo and was titled Hesana Qaghan; his rewards were lavish.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，以信義公主嫁焉，賜錦彩，袍千具、彩萬匹。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year Princess Xinyi was given to him in marriage, with gifts of brocades and satins—one thousand robes and ten thousand bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year Princess Xinyi was given to him in marriage, with one thousand brocade robes and ten thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 帝將復其故地，以遼東之役，故未遑也。

translations.literal: The emperor intended to restore his former territory, but because of the Liaodong campaign, had not yet had the leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to restore his old lands, but the Liaodong campaign left no time for it.

sentences.zh: 每從行幸。

translations.literal: He always accompanied the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: He always accompanied the emperor on tour.

sentences.zh: 江都之亂，隨化及至河北。

translations.literal: At the Jiangdu upheaval he followed Huaji to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiangdu upheaval he followed Huaji to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 化及將敗，奔歸京師，為北蕃突厥所害。

translations.literal: When Huaji was about to fall he fled back to the capital and was killed by the northern frontier Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji was near defeat he fled back to the capital and was killed by the northern Turks.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒之先，匈奴之苗裔也，

translations.literal: The ancestors of the Tiele were descendants of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele were descended from the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 種類最多，自西海之東依山據穀，往往不絕。

translations.literal: Their kinds were the most numerous; from east of the Western Sea they occupied valleys along the mountains, appearing everywhere without cease.
translations.idiomatic: They were the most numerous of peoples; from east of the Western Sea they held valleys along the mountains in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 獨洛河北，有僕骨、同羅、韋紇、拔也古、覆羅，並號俟斤，蒙陳、吐如紇、斯結、渾、斛薛等諸姓，勝兵可二萬。

translations.literal: North of the Duluo River were Pugu, Tongluo, Weihe, Bayegu, and Fuluo—all styled yabghu—along with the clans Mengchen, Turuhe, Sijie, Hun, Huxie, and others, with some twenty thousand fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Duluo River lived Pugu, Tongluo, Weihe, Bayegu, and Fuluo—all styled yabghu—plus the Mengchen, Turuhe, Sijie, Hun, Huxie, and other clans, with about twenty thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 伊吾以西，焉耆之北，傍白山，則有契弊、薄落職、乙栎至、蘇婆、那曷、烏護、紇骨、也栎至、於尼護等，勝兵可二萬。

translations.literal: West of Yiwu and north of Yanqi, beside Mount Bai, were Qibi, Boluozhi, Yilizhi, Supo, Nahe, Wuhu, Hegu, Yelizhi, Yunihu, and others, with some twenty thousand fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: West of Yiwu and north of Yanqi, beside Mount Bai, were Qibi, Boluozhi, Yilizhi, Supo, Nahe, Wuhu, Hegu, Yelizhi, Yunihu, and others, with about twenty thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 金山西南，有薛延阤、栎至勒兒、十盤、達契等，一萬餘兵。

translations.literal: Southwest of Mount Jin were Xueyantuo, Lizhile'er, Shipan, Daqi, and others, with more than ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of Mount Jin were Xueyantuo, Lizhile'er, Shipan, Daqi, and others, with more than ten thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 康國北，傍阿得水，則有訶栎至、曷截、撥忽、比干、具海、曷北悉、何嵯蘇、拔也末、謁達等，有三萬許兵。

translations.literal: North of Kangju, beside the Ashe River, were Helizhi, Hejie, Bohu, Bigan, Juhai, Hebeixi, Hezuosu, Bayemo, Yeda, and others, with about thirty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: North of Kangju, beside the Ashe River, were Helizhi, Hejie, Bohu, Bigan, Juhai, Hebeixi, Hezuosu, Bayemo, Yeda, and others, with about thirty thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 得嶷海東西，有蘇路羯、三素咽、篾促、薩忽等諸姓，八千餘。

translations.literal: East and west of Lake Telet were the clans Suluojie, Sansuoyan, Mietu, Sahu, and others, more than eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: East and west of Lake Telet were the Suluojie, Sansuoyan, Mietu, Sahu, and other clans, more than eight thousand strong.

sentences.zh: 拂菻東，則有恩屈、阿蘭、北褥、九離、伏嗢昏等，近二萬人。

translations.literal: East of Byzantium were Enqu, Alan, Beiru, Jiuli, Fu'uhun, and others, nearly twenty thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: East of Byzantium were Enqu, Alan, Beiru, Jiuli, Fu'uhun, and others, nearly twenty thousand people.

sentences.zh: 北海南，則都波等。

translations.literal: South of the Northern Sea were Dubo and others.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Northern Sea were the Dubo and others.

sentences.zh: 雖姓氏各別，總謂為鐵勒。

translations.literal: Though surnames differed in each case, collectively they were called the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Though their clan names differed, collectively they were called the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 並無君長，分屬東西兩突厥。

translations.literal: They all had no monarch but were divided between the Eastern and Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: They had no rulers of their own but were divided between the Eastern and Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 居無恆所，隨水草流移。

translations.literal: They had no fixed dwelling place but moved with the grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: They had no fixed abode but moved with pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 人性凶忍，善於騎射，貪婪尤甚，以寇抄為生。

translations.literal: Their nature was fierce and cruel; they were skilled at mounted archery, exceedingly greedy, and lived by raiding and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce and cruel, skilled horsemen and archers, exceedingly greedy, and lived by raiding.

sentences.zh: 近西邊者，頗為藝植，多牛而少馬。

translations.literal: Those near the western frontier did considerable agriculture and had many cattle but few horses.
translations.idiomatic: Those near the western frontier farmed somewhat and kept many cattle but few horses.

sentences.zh: 其俗大抵與突厥同。

translations.literal: Their customs were broadly the same as the Turks'.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were largely the same as the Turks'.

sentences.zh: 唯丈夫婚畢，便就妻家，待產乳男女，然後歸舍；

translations.literal: Only after a husband's marriage was complete he went to his wife's family, waited until she had borne and nursed children, and then returned to his own house;
translations.idiomatic: Only after marriage did a husband go to live with his wife's family until she had borne and nursed children, then return home;

sentences.zh: 死者埋殯之：此其異也。

translations.literal: the dead were buried in coffins—these were their differences.
translations.idiomatic: the dead were buried in coffins—these were their distinctive customs.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，遣使貢方物，自是不絕云。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye they sent envoys offering local products; from then tribute never ceased, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 3 they sent envoys with local goods; from then on tribute continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 論曰：四夷之為中國患也，久矣，北狄尤甚焉。

translations.literal: Commentary: The Four Barbarians as an affliction to China is of long standing; the Northern Di are especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The barbarians on the four sides have long been a scourge to China, and the northern peoples above all.

sentences.zh: 種落實繁，迭雄邊塞，年代遐邈，非一時也。

translations.literal: Their tribes are truly numerous; they have in succession been lords of the frontier passes; the ages stretch far back—not just one period.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribes are many; chiefs have risen in turn along the frontier over ages far beyond any single era.

sentences.zh: 五帝之世，則有獯鬻焉；

translations.literal: In the age of the Five Emperors there were the Xunyu;
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Five Emperors there were the Xunyu;

sentences.zh: 其在三代，則獫狁焉；

translations.literal: In the Three Dynasties there were the Xianyun;
translations.idiomatic: In the Three Dynasties there were the Xianyun;

sentences.zh: 逮乎兩漢，則匈奴焉；

translations.literal: Down to the Two Hans, there were the Xiongnu;
translations.idiomatic: In the Two Han dynasties there were the Xiongnu;

sentences.zh: 當塗、典午，則烏丸、鮮卑焉；

translations.literal: Under Dangtu and Dianwu there were the Wuhuan and Xianbei;
translations.idiomatic: Under Eastern Han and Jin there were the Wuhuan and Xianbei;

sentences.zh: 後魏及周，則蠕蠕、突厥。

translations.literal: Under Later Wei and Zhou, there were the Rouran and Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Wei and Zhou there were the Rouran and Turks.

sentences.zh: 此其酋豪相繼，互為君長者也。

translations.literal: These are their chieftains succeeding one another, each in turn becoming ruler.
translations.idiomatic: These were chieftains succeeding one another, each in turn becoming ruler.

sentences.zh: 皆以畜牧為業，侵抄為資，倏來忽往，雲飛鳥集。

translations.literal: All took livestock herding as their occupation and raiding as their sustenance, coming suddenly and going abruptly, like clouds flying and birds gathering.
translations.idiomatic: All lived by herding and raiding, appearing and vanishing like clouds and flocking birds.

sentences.zh: 智謀之士，議和親於廟堂之上；

translations.literal: Men of counsel debated marriage alliances in the hall of the temple;
translations.idiomatic: Counselors debated marriage alliances in the imperial court;

sentences.zh: 折沖之臣，論奮擊於塞垣之下。

translations.literal: Generals who repelled the enemy discussed striking boldly below the frontier walls.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier generals debated bold strikes below the border walls.

sentences.zh: 然事無恆規，權無定勢，親疏因其強弱，服叛在其盛衰，衰則款塞頓顙，盛則率兵寇掠。

translations.literal: Yet affairs had no constant rule, power no fixed tendency; closeness or distance followed their strength or weakness, submission or rebellion followed their rise or decline—when declining they came sincerely to the passes bowing heads; when thriving they led troops in raids.
translations.idiomatic: Yet nothing was fixed: friendship or estrangement followed strength and weakness, submission or rebellion followed rise and fall—when weak they came humbly to the passes; when strong they raided with armies.

sentences.zh: 屈伸異態。

translations.literal: Bending and stretching took different forms.
translations.idiomatic: Their posture shifted with circumstance.

sentences.zh: 強弱相反。

translations.literal: Strength and weakness reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Strength and weakness traded places.

sentences.zh: 正朔所不及，冠帶所不加。

translations.literal: Beyond the reach of the imperial calendar, outside the belt-and-cap civilization.
translations.idiomatic: They lay beyond the imperial calendar and the realm of court ritual.

sentences.zh: 唯利是視，不顧盟誓，至於莫相救護，驕黠憑陵。

translations.literal: They looked only to profit, heeded not oaths and pledges, to the point that they would not rescue one another, arrogant and cunning in encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: They cared only for gain, ignored oaths, would not aid one another, and grew arrogant and predatory.

sentences.zh: 和親結約之謀，行師用兵之事，前史論之備矣，故不詳而究焉。

translations.literal: The scheming of marriage alliances and treaties, the matters of marching armies and waging war—the former histories discuss them fully, so we do not treat them in detail here.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage alliances, treaties, campaigns, and battles are already fully treated in earlier histories, so they are not examined in detail here.

sentences.zh: 及蠕蠕衰微，突厥始大，至於木杆，遂雄朔野。

translations.literal: When the Rouran declined and weakened, the Turks first grew great; by Mugan, they dominated the northern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: As the Rouran declined, the Turks rose; under Mugan Qaghan they dominated the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 東極東胡舊境，西盡烏孫之地，彎弓數十萬，列處於代陰，南向以臨周、齊。

translations.literal: East they reached the old borders of the Donghu, west to the lands of the Wusun; bows bent by the hundreds of thousands, they arrayed themselves at Daiyin, facing south to overlook Zhou and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Their domain ran from the old Donghu lands in the east to Wusun territory in the west; with hundreds of thousands of bowmen they camped at Daiyin, facing south toward Zhou and Qi.

sentences.zh: 二國莫之能抗，爭請盟好，求結和親。

translations.literal: Neither realm could resist; both vied to request alliance and sought to conclude marriage ties.
translations.idiomatic: Neither state could stand against them; both sought alliance and marriage ties.

sentences.zh: 乃與周合從，終亡齊國。

translations.literal: Then allying with Zhou in joint accord, they in the end destroyed the Qi state.
translations.idiomatic: Allied with Zhou, they ultimately destroyed Qi.

sentences.zh: 隋文遷鼎，厥徒孔熾，負其眾力，將蹈秦郊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui moved the sacred tripod, their followers were very mighty; relying on their multitude they were about to tread the suburbs of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, the Turks were at their peak; trusting in their numbers, they threatened the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 內自相圖，遂以乖亂，達頭可汗遠遁，啟人願保塞下。

translations.literal: Internally they plotted against one another and fell into disorder; Qaghan Tatou fled far away, and Qiren wished to guard below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: They turned on one another and fell into chaos; Qaghan Tatou fled far away, and Qiren offered to guard the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 於是推亡固存，返其舊地，追討餘燼，部眾遂強，卒于仁壽，不侵不叛。

translations.literal: Thereupon, removing the doomed and securing what survived, his former lands were returned, the embers of the defeated pursued—his tribes then grew strong; by the end of the Renshou reign he neither invaded nor rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The court then restored what survived, returned his old lands, and pursued the defeated remnants—his tribes grew strong again; through the Renshou reign he neither invaded nor rebelled.

sentences.zh: 暨乎始畢，未虧臣禮。

translations.literal: Down to Shibi, he did not fall short in the rites of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Shibi, he did not fail in the duties of a vassal.

sentences.zh: 煬帝撫之非道，始有雁門之圍，俄屬群盜並與，於此浸以雄盛。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang handled them without the Way; first came the siege at Yanmen; soon bandit hosts rose everywhere, and from this they gradually grew mighty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang mishandled them; the siege at Yanmen followed, then rebel armies rose everywhere, and the Turks gradually grew mighty again.

sentences.zh: 豪傑雖建名號，莫不請好息人。

translations.literal: Though heroes established titles and names, none failed to request friendly ties and give the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: Even warlords who set up their own regimes all sought friendly ties with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 於是分置官司，總統中國，子女玉帛，相繼于道，使者之車，往來結轍。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were separately installed in office, presiding over China; daughters, sons, jade, and silks followed one after another on the roads, and envoys' carts came and went with wheels overlapping.
translations.idiomatic: They were given offices and authority over China; tribute of women, jade, and silk streamed along the roads, and envoys' carts crowded the highways.

sentences.zh: 自古蕃夷驕僭，未有若斯之甚也。

translations.literal: From antiquity the frontier barbarians' arrogance and presumption have never reached such an extreme as this.
translations.idiomatic: Never in antiquity had frontier peoples grown so arrogant and overreaching.

sentences.zh: 及聖哲應期，掃除氛祲。

translations.literal: When the sage and wise responded to the age, they swept away the baleful vapors.
translations.idiomatic: When a sage answered the times, the miasma was swept away.

sentences.zh: 暗于時變，猶懷抵拒，率其群醜，屢隳亭鄣，殘敗我雲、代，搖盪我太原，肆掠于涇陽，飲馬於渭汭。

translations.literal: Blind to the changing times, they still harbored resistance; leading their wicked host, they repeatedly destroyed frontier posts, ravaged our Yun and Dai, shook our Taiyuan, plundered at Jingyang, and watered their horses at the Wei ford.
translations.idiomatic: Blind to the turning age, they still resisted; leading their wicked bands they smashed frontier posts again and again, ravaged Yun and Dai, shook Taiyuan, plundered Jingyang, and watered their horses at the Wei ford.

sentences.zh: 太宗文皇帝奇謀內運，神機密動，遂使百世不羈之虜，一舉而滅。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong the Cultured Emperor, with wondrous stratagems working within and divine schemes moving in secret, thereby caused the barbarians unrestrained for a hundred generations to be destroyed in a single stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, with wondrous stratagems within and secret divine moves, destroyed in one stroke a foe that had run wild for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 瀚海龍庭之地，盡為九州；

translations.literal: The lands of the Hanhai and Longting all became the Nine Provinces;
translations.idiomatic: The Hanhai and Longting became part of the Nine Provinces;

sentences.zh: 幽都窮發之鄉，隸於編戶。

translations.literal: the lands of Youdu and Qiongfa were entered in the household registers.
translations.idiomatic: the far north of Youdu and Qiongfa was entered on the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 實帝皇所不及，書契所未聞。

translations.literal: Truly this was what emperors could not achieve and what written records had never recorded.
translations.idiomatic: What no emperor had achieved and no chronicle had ever recorded.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，雖天道有盛衰，亦人事之工拙也。

translations.literal: Speaking from this, though the Way of Heaven has waxing and waning, it is also a matter of human effort—skill or clumsiness.
translations.idiomatic: From this we see that though Heaven's mandate waxes and wanes, human effort—skill or folly—matters too.

sentences.zh: 加以為而弗恃，有而弗居，類天地之含容，同陰陽之化育，斯乃大道之行也，固無得而稱焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, he acted yet did not rely on it, possessed yet did not dwell in it—like Heaven and Earth's forbearance, like yin and yang's nurturing; this is the conduct of the Great Way, and truly there is no fitting way to praise it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he achieved yet did not boast, possessed yet did not cling—like Heaven and Earth in forbearance, like yin and yang in nurture; such is the Great Way in action, beyond all praise.
